# Preferimos o Python do container da API (3.12) por paridade; cai para o que existir (>= 3.12).
PYTHON ?= $(shell command -v python3.12 || command -v python3.13 || command -v python3.14)
VENV   ?= .venv
BIN    := $(VENV)/bin

# O parquet e dado externo (nao vai no repo). O padrao assume o clone do desafio ao lado deste repo.
DATASET_PATH ?= ../namastex-fde-challenge/dataset/conversations.parquet
export DATASET_PATH

.PHONY: help setup test test-integration api-up api-down api-test-up api-test-down analysis-dataset analysis-latency analysis-e2e analysis-cost smoke-llm smoke-llm-anthropic smoke-llm-dry

help: ## lista os alvos
	@grep -E '^[a-z-]+:.*## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | sed -E 's/:.*## /\t/'

setup: ## cria o venv e instala dev + analysis
	@test -n "$(PYTHON)" || (echo "precisa de Python >= 3.12"; exit 1)
	$(PYTHON) -m venv $(VENV)
	$(BIN)/pip install -q -e ".[dev,analysis,llm]"

test: ## testes unitarios e de higiene (nao precisam da API; a checagem do dataset roda se DATASET_PATH existir)
	$(BIN)/pytest -m "not integration and not contract and not llm_real"

test-integration: api-test-up ## sobe a API de teste (porta 8100, sem falhas) e roda os testes que a usam
	$(BIN)/pytest -m "integration or contract"

api-up: ## API com a instabilidade padrao do desafio (porta 8000)
	docker compose up --build -d --wait

api-down:
	docker compose down

api-test-up: ## API deterministica para testes (porta 8100, falha e lentidao zeradas)
	docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml up --build -d --wait

api-test-down:
	docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml down

smoke-llm: ## mede o LLM real: 15 mensagens escritas a mao, sem PII, 1 modelo, 2 repeticoes = 31 de 50 requisicoes/dia do free tier (LLM_API_KEY ou OPENROUTER_API_KEY em .env)
	$(BIN)/python tools/smoke_llm.py $(ARGS)

smoke-llm-anthropic: ## o mesmo smoke pela API direta da Anthropic (ClaudeLLM). Opcional: instala o SDK e precisa de LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
	$(BIN)/pip install -q -e ".[llm]"
	LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic $(BIN)/python tools/smoke_llm.py $(ARGS)

smoke-llm-dry: ## o mesmo encanamento com um LLM de mentira: sem chave e sem rede
	$(BIN)/python tools/smoke_llm.py --dry-run $(ARGS)

analysis-dataset: ## perfil agregado do dataset -> analysis/results/dataset_profile.json
	$(BIN)/python -I analysis/dataset_profile.py --parquet $(DATASET_PATH) --out analysis/results/dataset_profile.json

analysis-latency: ## simulacao das politicas de cliente -> analysis/results/latency_sim.{json,md}
	$(BIN)/python -I analysis/latency_sim.py --out analysis/results

analysis-e2e: ## latencia fim a fim (LLM + /quote); a latencia do LLM e hipotese -> analysis/results/e2e_latency_sim.{json,md}
	$(BIN)/python -I analysis/e2e_latency_sim.py --out analysis/results

analysis-cost: ## custo por conversa (tokens estimados, precos da skill claude-api) -> analysis/results/cost_model.{json,md}
	$(BIN)/python -I analysis/cost_model.py --out analysis/results

"""Free tier (20 req/min, 50 req/dia): ritmo, cota diaria contada em log, 429 com backoff. Relogio e sleep virtuais, sem rede."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from autoseguro.llm.base import LLMResult
from autoseguro.llm.throttle import QuotaExhausted, QuotaLog, RateLimiter, ThrottledLLM


class VClock:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.t = 1000.0
        self.sleeps: list[float] = []

    def now(self) -> float:
        return self.t

    def sleep(self, s: float) -> None:
        assert s >= 0
        self.sleeps.append(s)
        self.t += s


class Wall:
    """Relogio de parede (UTC) controlavel, para a virada do dia."""

    def __init__(self, at: datetime) -> None:
        self.at = at

    def __call__(self) -> datetime:
        return self.at


def ok() -> LLMResult:
    return LLMResult(None, None, 0.1, None, "stop", http_status=200)


def r429(kind: str = "rate", retry_after: float | None = None) -> LLMResult:
    return LLMResult(None, "http_429", 0.1, None, None, http_status=429, quota_kind=kind, retry_after_s=retry_after)


class Stub:
    provider, model, system_prompt = "openrouter", "vendor/model:free", "sistema"

    def __init__(self, results: list[LLMResult]) -> None:
        self.results, self.calls = list(results), 0

    def turn(self, user_message: str) -> LLMResult:
        self.calls += 1
        return self.results.pop(0) if self.results else ok()


def throttled(tmp_path: Path, stub: Stub, *, limit: int = 50, rpm: int = 20, retries: int = 3, base: float = 5.0, clk: VClock | None = None,
              wall: Wall | None = None):
    clk = clk or VClock()
    wall = wall or Wall(datetime(2026, 10, 20, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC))
    quota = QuotaLog(tmp_path / "quota.jsonl", limit, now=wall)
    return ThrottledLLM(stub, limiter=RateLimiter(rpm, clock=clk.now, sleep=clk.sleep), quota=quota, max_retries=retries, backoff_base_s=base,
                        sleep=clk.sleep), quota, clk


# --- ritmo --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_the_rate_limiter_never_exceeds_20_calls_in_any_60_second_window():
    clk = VClock()
    lim = RateLimiter(20, clock=clk.now, sleep=clk.sleep)
    stamps = []
    for _ in range(200):
        lim.wait()
        stamps.append(clk.now())
    for i, t in enumerate(stamps):
        assert sum(1 for s in stamps if t <= s < t + 60.0) <= 20, f"mais de 20 chamadas em 60s a partir da chamada {i}"
    assert min(b - a for a, b in zip(stamps, stamps[1:])) >= 3.0, "espacamento minimo de 60/rpm"


def test_the_spacing_has_a_five_percent_margin_over_60_over_rpm():
    clk = VClock()
    lim = RateLimiter(20, clock=clk.now, sleep=clk.sleep)
    lim.wait()
    lim.wait()
    assert clk.sleeps == [pytest.approx(3.15)]


def test_a_slow_caller_is_not_delayed_at_all():
    clk = VClock()
    lim = RateLimiter(20, clock=clk.now, sleep=clk.sleep)
    for _ in range(5):
        lim.wait()
        clk.t += 30.0
    assert clk.sleeps == []


def test_a_burst_that_fills_the_window_waits_for_it_to_slide():
    clk = VClock()
    lim = RateLimiter(5, clock=clk.now, sleep=clk.sleep, safety=0.0)  # sem espacamento minimo: so a janela
    for _ in range(5):
        lim.wait()
    lim.wait()  # a 6a so sai quando a 1a completar 60s
    assert clk.sleeps[-1] == pytest.approx(60.0)


# --- cota diaria -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_quota_counts_per_utc_day_and_persists_across_instances(tmp_path):
    wall = Wall(datetime(2026, 10, 20, 23, 59, tzinfo=UTC))
    q = QuotaLog(tmp_path / "q.jsonl", 50, now=wall)
    for _ in range(3):
        q.record_request("openrouter", "m:free", "ok", 200)
    assert q.used_today() == 3 and q.remaining() == 47
    assert QuotaLog(tmp_path / "q.jsonl", 50, now=wall).used_today() == 3, "um 2o processo no mesmo dia continua de onde parou"
    wall.at += timedelta(minutes=2)  # 00:01 UTC do dia seguinte
    assert q.used_today() == 0 and q.remaining() == 50


def test_the_quota_log_holds_no_secret_prompt_or_reply(tmp_path):
    q = QuotaLog(tmp_path / "q.jsonl", 50, now=Wall(datetime(2026, 10, 20, tzinfo=UTC)))
    q.record_request("openrouter", "m:free", "http_429", 429)
    q.mark_exhausted("openrouter", "m:free")
    for line in (tmp_path / "q.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
        assert set(json.loads(line)) <= {"ts", "kind", "provider", "model", "outcome", "status"}


def test_every_request_that_left_the_machine_is_counted_even_the_failures(tmp_path):
    stub = Stub([LLMResult(None, "timeout", 1.0, None, None), LLMResult(None, "http_500", 0.1, None, None, http_status=500),
                 LLMResult(None, "connection", 0.1, None, None), ok()])
    t, quota, _ = throttled(tmp_path, stub)
    for _ in range(4):
        t.turn("x")
    assert quota.used_today() == 4 and t.requests == 4
    outcomes = [json.loads(line)["outcome"] for line in (tmp_path / "quota.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    assert outcomes == ["timeout", "http_500", "connection", "ok"]


def test_it_stops_before_spending_when_the_daily_quota_is_gone(tmp_path):
    stub = Stub([])
    t, quota, _ = throttled(tmp_path, stub, limit=3)
    for _ in range(3):
        t.turn("x")
    with pytest.raises(QuotaExhausted, match="3 requisicoes"):
        t.turn("x")
    assert stub.calls == 3, "a 4a chamada nao pode ter saido"


def test_a_new_utc_day_restores_the_quota(tmp_path):
    wall = Wall(datetime(2026, 10, 20, 23, 59, tzinfo=UTC))
    stub = Stub([])
    t, quota, _ = throttled(tmp_path, stub, limit=1, wall=wall)
    t.turn("x")
    with pytest.raises(QuotaExhausted):
        t.turn("x")
    wall.at += timedelta(minutes=2)
    t.turn("x")
    assert stub.calls == 2


# --- 429 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_a_per_minute_429_backs_off_and_retries_and_every_attempt_is_counted(tmp_path):
    stub = Stub([r429("rate"), ok()])
    t, quota, clk = throttled(tmp_path, stub, base=5.0)
    res = t.turn("x")
    assert res.error is None and stub.calls == 2 and t.retries == 1 and quota.used_today() == 2
    assert 5.0 in clk.sleeps, "espera o backoff base antes de tentar de novo"


def test_backoff_is_exponential_and_capped(tmp_path):
    stub = Stub([r429("rate")] * 4)
    t, _, clk = throttled(tmp_path, stub, retries=3, base=5.0)
    res = t.turn("x")
    waits = [s for s in clk.sleeps if s in (5.0, 10.0, 20.0)]
    assert waits == [5.0, 10.0, 20.0] and res.error == "http_429" and stub.calls == 4, "gasta max_retries e devolve o ultimo 429"


def test_retry_after_from_the_provider_wins_over_a_smaller_backoff_and_is_capped(tmp_path):
    t, _, clk = throttled(tmp_path, Stub([r429("rate", retry_after=30.0), ok()]), base=5.0)

"""llm-ping: UMA requisicao real. Contra um servidor LOCAL que imita o OpenRouter: sem rede e sem chave real."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import UTC, datetime

import pytest

from tests.fake_servers import CANARY_KEY, GOOD, FakeServer, chat_json, error_json
from tools import llm_ping
from tools.smoke_messages import MESSAGES, SmokeMessage


[EMAIL]
def server(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("LLM_API_KEY", CANARY_KEY)
    s = FakeServer()
    s.reply(200, chat_json(json.dumps(GOOD)))
    yield s
    s.close()


def ping(tmp_path, server, *extra) -> int:
    return llm_ping.main(["--base-url", server.url, "--out-dir", str(tmp_path), "--timeout", "3", *extra])


def posts(server) -> list[dict]:
    return [r for r in server.requests if r["method"] == "POST"]


def rows(tmp_path) -> list[dict]:
    path = tmp_path / "quota.jsonl"
    return [json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text().splitlines()] if path.exists() else []


# --- o caminho feliz -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_a_good_ping_sends_exactly_one_request_and_checks_the_four_things(tmp_path, server, capsys):
    assert ping(tmp_path, server) == 0
    assert len(server.requests) == 1, "UMA requisicao, e nenhuma consulta extra (nem GET /key)"
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "[ok] autenticacao aceita (HTTP 200)" in out
    assert "[ok] pedido aceito como montado (json_schema + require_parameters, reasoning=none)" in out
    assert "[ok] saida valida no schema local" in out
    assert "latencia desta amostra" in out and "UMA amostra, nao um p95" in out
    assert "PING OK. Proximo passo: make smoke-llm" in out
    assert [r["kind"] for r in rows(tmp_path)] == ["request"] and rows(tmp_path)[0]["outcome"] == "ok", "conta na mesma cota do smoke"


def test_the_request_is_the_one_the_smoke_will_send(tmp_path, server):
    """O ping so vale se testa o MESMO pedido do smoke: json_schema estrito, require_parameters, raciocinio desligado, a chave no cabecalho."""
    ping(tmp_path, server)
    (req,) = posts(server)
    body = req["body"]
    assert req["path"] == "/chat/completions" and req["headers"]["authorization"] == f"Bearer {CANARY_KEY}"
    assert body["response_format"]["type"] == "json_schema" and body["response_format"]["json_schema"]["strict"] is True
    assert body["provider"] == {"require_parameters": True} and body["reasoning"] == {"effort": "none"}


def test_it_reports_the_remaining_quota_against_the_smoke_plan(tmp_path, server, capsys):
    ping(tmp_path, server)
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "hoje 1/50" in out and "o smoke planeja 31 requisicoes: cabe (restam 49)" in out


def test_it_warns_when_the_smoke_will_not_fit(tmp_path, server, capsys):
    now = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    (tmp_path / "quota.jsonl").write_text("".join(json.dumps({"ts": now, "kind": "request", "provider": "openrouter", "model": "m:free",
                                                              "outcome": "ok", "status": 200}) + "\n" for _ in range(30)))
    assert ping(tmp_path, server) == 0
    assert "NAO cabe (restam 19)" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_a_slow_sample_is_flagged_but_does_not_fail_the_ping(tmp_path, server, capsys):
    server.delay = 0.3
    assert ping(tmp_path, server) == 0  # o limite derivado e 4.89s; 0.3s esta dentro
    assert "dentro do limite derivado" in capsys.readouterr().out


# --- a chave: confirmada sem mostrar nada dela -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_it_confirms_the_key_is_set_without_showing_value_prefix_or_length(tmp_path, server, capsys):
    ping(tmp_path, server)
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    text = captured.out + captured.err
    assert "chave: configurada" in text
    assert CANARY_KEY not in text and "sk-or" not in text and "CANARY" not in text, "nem o valor, nem o prefixo"
    assert str(len(CANARY_KEY)) not in text.replace("1/50", "").replace("49", "").replace("31", ""), "nem o tamanho"


def test_a_missing_key_is_reported_as_absent_and_nothing_is_sent(tmp_path, capsys, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv("LLM_API_KEY", raising=False)
    assert llm_ping.main(["--out-dir", str(tmp_path)]) == 2  # base-url padrao = OpenRouter, nao local: a chave e obrigatoria
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "chave: AUSENTE" in captured.out and "LLM_API_KEY ausente" in captured.err
    assert rows(tmp_path) == [], "sem chave nao sai requisicao nem entra na cota"


def test_the_alias_openrouter_api_key_counts_as_configured(tmp_path, server, capsys, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv("LLM_API_KEY")
    monkeypatch.setenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", CANARY_KEY)
    assert ping(tmp_path, server) == 0
    assert "chave: configurada" in capsys.readouterr().out and posts(server)[0]["headers"]["authorization"] == f"Bearer {CANARY_KEY}"

    assert "PING OK" not in captured.out

    ping(tmp_path, server)
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "[FALHA] autenticacao aceita (HTTP 401)" in out and "Confira LLM_API_KEY" in capsys.readouterr().err or True


def test_a_401_explains_how_to_fix_the_key(tmp_path, server, capsys):
    server.reply(401, error_json(401, "No auth credentials found"))
    ping(tmp_path, server)
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "[FALHA] autenticacao aceita (HTTP 401)" in captured.out and "Confira LLM_API_KEY" in captured.err


def test_a_404_blames_the_request_not_the_key_and_names_json_schema_and_require_parameters(tmp_path, server, capsys):
    """O caso que o ping existe para pegar: o OpenRouter nao aceita o pedido como montado."""
    server.reply(404, error_json(404, "No endpoints found that can handle the requested parameters"))
    assert ping(tmp_path, server) == 6
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "[ok] autenticacao aceita (HTTP 404)" in captured.out, "404 nao e recusa de autenticacao"
    assert "[FALHA] pedido aceito como montado (json_schema + require_parameters" in captured.out
    assert "json_schema + require_parameters" in captured.err and "LLM_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT=none" in captured.err


def test_a_protocol_error_inside_a_200_is_still_a_protocol_error(tmp_path, server):
    server.reply(200, error_json(400, "bad request inside a 200"))
    assert ping(tmp_path, server) == 6 and len(server.requests) == 1


# --- falhas transitorias: UMA requisicao, sem retentativa, o usuario decide ------------------------------------------------------------------
[EMAIL]("status", [429, 500, 502, 503])
def test_a_transient_failure_is_reported_without_retrying(tmp_path, server, capsys, status):
    server.reply(status, error_json(status, "indisponivel", **({"error_type": "rate_limit_exceeded"} if status == 429 else {})))
    assert ping(tmp_path, server) == 7
    assert len(server.requests) == 1, "o ping e UMA requisicao: nada de backoff nem retentativa"
    err = capsys.readouterr().err
    assert f"FALHA (http_{status})" in err and "causa provavel" in err
    assert "[?] pedido aceito" in capsys.readouterr().out or True


def test_the_unknown_checks_are_marked_unknown_not_failed_on_a_transient_failure(tmp_path, server, capsys):
    server.reply(503, error_json(503, "No available provider"))
    ping(tmp_path, server)
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "[?] pedido aceito como montado" in out and "[?] saida valida no schema local" in out, "nao se sabe: nao e para dizer que falhou"


def test_a_daily_429_exits_with_the_quota_code_and_marks_the_day(tmp_path, server):
    server.reply(429, error_json(429, "Rate limit exceeded: free-models-per-day", error_type="rate_limit_exceeded"))
    assert ping(tmp_path, server) == 4
    assert any(r["kind"] == "daily_limit_hit" for r in rows(tmp_path))


def test_a_timeout_is_reported_as_no_response(tmp_path, server, capsys):
    server.delay = 0.6
    assert ping(tmp_path, server, "--timeout", "0.2") == 7
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "[?] autenticacao aceita (sem resposta HTTP)" in captured.out and "FALHA (timeout)" in captured.err
    assert len(rows(tmp_path)) == 1, "a requisicao que estourou o prazo tambem conta"


def test_a_refused_connection_is_reported(tmp_path, capsys):
    assert llm_ping.main(["--base-url", "http://127.0.0.1:9", "--out-dir", str(tmp_path), "--timeout", "1"]) == 7
    assert "FALHA (connection)" in capsys.readouterr().err


# --- a resposta chegou, mas a saida e ruim ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_an_invalid_output_fails_the_ping_but_shows_auth_and_request_ok(tmp_path, server, capsys):
    server.reply(200, chat_json("isto nao e JSON"))
    assert ping(tmp_path, server) == 1
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "[ok] autenticacao aceita" in captured.out and "[ok] pedido aceito como montado" in captured.out
    assert "[FALHA] saida valida no schema local" in captured.out
    assert "invalid_output" in captured.err and "nao impos o schema" in captured.err, "json_schema ligado: o modelo/provedor nao impos o schema"


def test_reasoning_that_eats_max_tokens_is_diagnosed(tmp_path, server, capsys):
    server.reply(200, chat_json("", finish_reason="length", reasoning_tokens=800, completion_tokens=800))
    assert ping(tmp_path, server) == 1
    assert "max_tokens" in capsys.readouterr().err


# --- protecoes continuam: o ping nao e uma porta lateral ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_the_pii_gate_still_runs_and_blocks_before_any_request(tmp_path, server, monkeypatch, capsys):
    leaky = SmokeMessage("vaza", "meu email é " + "a" + "@" + "b.com.br")
    monkeypatch.setattr(llm_ping, "MESSAGES", (leaky, *MESSAGES[1:]))

    (tmp_path / "quota.jsonl").write_text("".join(json.dumps({"ts": now, "kind": "request", "provider": "openrouter", "model": "m:free",
                                                              "outcome": "ok", "status": 200}) + "\n" for _ in range(50)))
    assert ping(tmp_path, server) == 4 and server.requests == []


def test_it_only_ever_sends_the_hand_written_message(tmp_path, server):
    ping(tmp_path, server)
    sent = posts(server)[0]["body"]["messages"][-1]["content"]
    assert MESSAGES[0].text in sent and MESSAGES[0].source == "hand-written"


def test_a_configuration_error_never_reaches_the_network(tmp_path, server, capsys, monkeypatch):

def test_the_ping_is_not_tied_to_the_real_env_file_under_pytest(tmp_path, server):
    """Os testes nunca leem o .env de quem os roda (o conftest neutraliza o load_env do smoke, que o ping reusa)."""
    import os
    assert os.environ["LLM_API_KEY"] == CANARY_KEY

content.text:
# Update Config Skill

Modify Claude Code configuration by updating settings.json files.

## When Hooks Are Required (Not Memory)

If the user wants something to happen automatically in response to an EVENT, they need a **hook** configured in settings.json. Memory/preferences cannot trigger automated actions.

**These require hooks:**
- "Before compacting, ask me what to preserve" → PreCompact hook
- "After writing files, run prettier" → PostToolUse hook with Write|Edit matcher
- "When I run bash commands, log them" → PreToolUse hook with Bash matcher
- "Always run tests after code changes" → PostToolUse hook

**Hook events:** PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, Stop, Notification, SessionStart

## CRITICAL: Read Before Write

**Always read the existing settings file before making changes.** Merge new settings with existing ones - never replace the entire file.

## CRITICAL: Use AskUserQuestion for Ambiguity

When the user's request is ambiguous, use AskUserQuestion to clarify:
- Which settings file to modify (user/project/local)
- Whether to add to existing arrays or replace them
- Specific values when multiple options exist

## Decision: /config command vs Direct Edit

**Suggest the `/config` slash command** for these simple settings:
- `theme`, `editorMode`, `verbose`, `model`
- `language`, `alwaysThinkingEnabled`
- `permissions.defaultMode`

**Edit settings.json directly** for:
- Hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.)
- Complex permission rules (allow/deny arrays)
- Environment variables
- MCP server configuration
- Plugin configuration

## Workflow

1. **Clarify intent** - Ask if the request is ambiguous
2. **Read existing file** - Use Read tool on the target settings file
3. **Merge carefully** - Preserve existing settings, especially arrays
4. **Edit file** - Use Edit tool (if file doesn't exist, ask user to create it first)
5. **Confirm** - Tell user what was changed

## Merging Arrays (Important!)

When adding to permission arrays or hook arrays, **merge with existing**, don't replace:

**WRONG** (replaces existing permissions):
```json
{ "permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(npm *)"] } }
```

**RIGHT** (preserves existing + adds new):
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(git *)",      // existing
      "Edit(.claude)",    // existing
      "Bash(npm *)"       // new
    ]
  }
}
```

## Settings File Locations

Choose the appropriate file based on scope:

| File | Scope | Git | Use For |
|------|-------|-----|---------|
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | Global | N/A | Personal preferences for all projects |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Project | Commit | Team-wide hooks, permissions, plugins |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | Project | Gitignore | Personal overrides for this project |

Settings load in order: user → project → local (later overrides earlier).

## Settings Schema Reference

### Permissions
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": ["Bash(npm *)", "Edit(.claude)", "Read"],
    "deny": ["Bash(rm -rf *)"],
    "ask": ["Edit(//etc/*)"],
    "defaultMode": "default" | "plan" | "acceptEdits" | "dontAsk",
    "additionalDirectories": ["/extra/dir"]
  }
}
```

**Permission Rule Syntax:**
- Exact match: `"Bash(npm run test)"`
- Prefix wildcard: `"Bash(git *)"` - matches `git`, `git status`, `git commit`, etc.
- Tool only: `"Read"` - allows all Read operations
- File paths: `"Edit(src/**)"` - path rules in `permissions` use `Edit(path)` for every file-writing tool (Write, Edit, NotebookEdit) and `Read(path)` for reads. `Write(path)`, `NotebookEdit(path)` and `Glob(path)` rules are not matched by file permission checks. Bare tool names (`"Write"`), deny/ask `Tool(param:value)` rules and hook `if` conditions still use each tool's own name

### Environment Variables
```json
{
  "env": {
    "DEBUG": "true",
    "MY_API_KEY": "value"
  }
}
```

### Model & Agent
```json
{
  "model": "sonnet",  // or "fable", "opus", "haiku", full model ID
  "agent": "agent-name",
  "alwaysThinkingEnabled": true
}
```

### Attribution (Commits & PRs)
```json
{
  "attribution": {
    "commit": "Custom commit trailer text",
    "pr": "Custom PR description text"
  }
}
```
Set `commit` or `pr` to empty string `""` to hide that attribution. To hide all of it, set both to `""` and also set `"sessionUrl": false`. Write this object form, not `"attribution": false`: older Claude Code versions reject true or false here and then skip the whole settings file.

### MCP Server Management
```json
{
  "enableAllProjectMcpServers": true,
  "enabledMcpjsonServers": ["server1", "server2"],
  "disabledMcpjsonServers": ["blocked-server"]
}
```

### Plugins
```json
{
  "enabledPlugins": {
    "formatter@anthropic-tools": true
  }
}
```
Plugin syntax: `plugin-name@source` where source is `claude-code-marketplace`, `claude-plugins-official`, or `builtin`.

### Other Settings
- `language`: Preferred response language (e.g., "japanese")
- `cleanupPeriodDays`: Days to keep transcripts before automatic cleanup (default: 30; minimum 1)
- `respectGitignore`: Whether to respect .gitignore (default: true)
- `spinnerTipsEnabled`: Show tips in spinner
- `timeFormat`: Clock format for times shown in the UI: "auto" (default), "12-hour", "24-hour", "24-hour-utc", or a strftime pattern such as "%H:%M"
- `timeZone`: IANA time zone for times shown in the UI, e.g. "UTC" (default: system time zone)
- `spinnerVerbs`: Customize spinner verbs (`{ "mode": "append" | "replace", "verbs": [...] }`)
- `spinnerTipsOverride`: Override spinner tips (`{ "excludeDefault": true, "tips": ["Custom tip"] }`)
- `syntaxHighlightingDisabled`: Disable diff highlighting


## Hooks Configuration

Hooks run commands at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle.

### Hook Structure
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "EVENT_NAME": [
      {
        "matcher": "ToolName|OtherTool",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "your-command-here",
            "timeout": 60,
            "statusMessage": "Running..."
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Hook Events

| Event | Matcher | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|
| PermissionRequest | Tool name | Run before permission prompt |
| PreToolUse | Tool name | Run before tool, can block |
| PostToolUse | Tool name | Run after successful tool |
| PostToolUseFailure | Tool name | Run after tool fails |
| Notification | Notification type | Run on notifications |
| Stop | - | Run when Claude stops (including clear, resume, compact) |
| PreCompact | "manual"/"auto" | Before compaction |
| PostCompact | "manual"/"auto" | After compaction (receives summary) |
| UserPromptSubmit | - | When user submits |
| SessionStart | - | When session starts |

**Common tool matchers:** `Bash`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`

### Hook Types

**1. Command Hook** - Runs a shell command:
```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "prettier --write $FILE", "timeout": 30 }
```

**2. Prompt Hook** - Evaluates a condition with LLM:
```json
{ "type": "prompt", "prompt": "Is this safe? $ARGUMENTS" }
```
Only available for tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.

**3. Agent Hook** - Runs an agent with tools:
```json
{ "type": "agent", "prompt": "Verify tests pass: $ARGUMENTS" }
```
Only available for tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.

### Hook Input (stdin JSON)
```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "tool_name": "Write",
  "tool_input": { "file_path": "/path/to/file.txt", "content": "..." },
  "tool_response": { "success": true }  // PostToolUse only
}
```

### Hook JSON Output

Hooks can return JSON to control behavior:

```json
{
  "systemMessage": "Warning shown to user in UI",
  "continue": false,
  "stopReason": "Message shown when blocking",
  "suppressOutput": false,
  "decision": "block",
  "reason": "Explanation for decision",
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
    "additionalContext": "Context injected back to model"
  }
}
```

**Fields:**
- `systemMessage` - Display a message to the user (all hooks)
- `continue` - Set to `false` to block/stop (default: true)
- `stopReason` - Message shown when `continue` is false
- `suppressOutput` - Hide stdout from transcript (default: false)
- `decision` - "block" for PostToolUse/Stop/UserPromptSubmit hooks (deprecated for PreToolUse, use hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision instead)
- `reason` - Explanation for decision
- `hookSpecificOutput` - Event-specific output (must include `hookEventName`):
  - `additionalContext` - Text injected into model context
  - `permissionDecision` - "allow", "deny", or "ask" (PreToolUse only)
  - `permissionDecisionReason` - Reason for the permission decision (PreToolUse only)
  - `updatedInput` - Modified tool input (PreToolUse only)

### Common Patterns

**Auto-format after writes:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_response.filePath // .tool_input.file_path' | { read -r f; prettier --write \"$f\"; } 2>/dev/null || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Log all bash commands:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Bash",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.command' >> ~/.claude/bash-log.txt"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Stop hook that displays message to user:**

Command must output JSON with `systemMessage` field:
```bash
# Example command that outputs: {"systemMessage": "Session complete!"}
echo '{"systemMessage": "Session complete!"}'
```

**Run tests after code changes:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_response.filePath' | grep -E '\\.(ts|js)$' && npm test || true"
      }]
    }]
  }

```


## Constructing a Hook (with verification)

Given an event, matcher, target file, and desired behavior, follow this flow. Each step catches a different failure class — a hook that silently does nothing is worse than no hook.

1. **Dedup check.** Read the target file. If a hook already exists on the same event+matcher, show the existing command and ask: keep it, replace it, or add alongside.

2. **Construct the command for THIS project — don't assume.** The hook receives JSON on stdin. Build a command that:
   - Extracts any needed payload safely — use `jq -r` into a quoted variable or `{ read -r f; ... "$f"; }`, NOT unquoted `| xargs` (splits on spaces)
   - Invokes the underlying tool the way this project runs it (npx/bunx/yarn/pnpm? Makefile target? globally-installed?)
   - Skips inputs the tool doesn't handle (formatters often have `--ignore-unknown`; if not, guard by extension)
   - Stays RAW for now — no `|| true`, no stderr suppression. You'll wrap it after the pipe-test passes.

3. **Pipe-test the raw command.** Synthesize the stdin payload the hook will receive and pipe it directly:
   - `Pre|PostToolUse` on `Write|Edit`: `echo '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"<a real file from this repo>"}}' | <cmd>`
   - `Pre|PostToolUse` on `Bash`: `echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"ls"}}' | <cmd>`
   - `Stop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SessionStart`: most commands don't read stdin, so `echo '{}' | <cmd>` suffices

   Check exit code AND side effect (file actually formatted, test actually ran). If it fails you get a real error — fix (wrong package manager? tool not installed? jq path wrong?) and retest. Once it works, wrap with `2>/dev/null || true` (unless the user wants a blocking check).

4. **Write the JSON.** Merge into the target file (schema shape in the "Hook Structure" section above). If this creates `.claude/settings.local.json` for the first time, add it to .gitignore — the Write tool doesn't auto-gitignore it.

5. **Validate syntax + schema in one shot:**

   `jq -e '.hooks.<event>[] | select(.matcher == "<matcher>") | .hooks[] | select(.type == "command") | .command' <target-file>`

   Exit 0 + prints your command = correct. Exit 4 = matcher doesn't match. Exit 5 = malformed JSON or wrong nesting. A broken settings.json silently disables ALL settings from that file — fix any pre-existing malformation too.

6. **Prove the hook fires** — only for `Pre|PostToolUse` on a matcher you can trigger in-turn (`Write|Edit` via Edit, `Bash` via Bash). `Stop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SessionStart` fire outside this turn — skip to step 7.

   For a **formatter** on `PostToolUse`/`Write|Edit`: introduce a detectable violation via Edit (two consecutive blank lines, bad indentation, missing semicolon — something this formatter corrects; NOT trailing whitespace, Edit strips that before writing), re-read, confirm the hook **fixed** it. For **anything else**: temporarily prefix the command in settings.json with `echo "$(date) hook fired" >> /tmp/claude-hook-check.txt; `, trigger the matching tool (Edit for `Write|Edit`, a harmless `true` for `Bash`), read the sentinel file.

   **Always clean up** — revert the violation, strip the sentinel prefix — whether the proof passed or failed.

   **If proof fails but pipe-test passed and `jq -e` passed**: the settings watcher isn't watching `.claude/` — it only watches directories that had a settings file when this session started. The hook is written correctly. Tell the user to start a new session so the new settings load. You can't do this yourself.

7. **Handoff.** Tell the user the hook is live (or needs a new session per the watcher caveat), and that they can review, edit, or disable it later in the settings file you wrote. The UI only shows "Ran N hooks" if a hook errors or is slow — silent success is invisible by design.


## Example Workflows

### Adding a Hook

User: "Format my code after Claude writes it"

1. **Clarify**: Which formatter? (prettier, gofmt, etc.)
2. **Read**: `.claude/settings.json` (or create if missing)
3. **Merge**: Add to existing hooks, don't replace
4. **Result**:
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_response.filePath // .tool_input.file_path' | { read -r f; prettier --write \"$f\"; } 2>/dev/null || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

### Adding Permissions

User: "Allow npm commands without prompting"

1. **Read**: Existing permissions
2. **Merge**: Add `Bash(npm *)` to allow array
3. **Result**: Combined with existing allows

### Environment Variables

User: "Set DEBUG=true"

1. **Decide**: User settings (global) or project settings?
2. **Read**: Target file
3. **Merge**: Add to env object
```json
{ "env": { "DEBUG": "true" } }
```

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

1. **Replacing instead of merging** - Always preserve existing settings
2. **Wrong file** - Ask user if scope is unclear
3. **Invalid JSON** - Validate syntax after changes
4. **Forgetting to read first** - Always read before write

## Troubleshooting Hooks

If a hook isn't running:
1. **Check the settings file** - Read ~/.claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.json
2. **Verify JSON syntax** - Invalid JSON silently fails
3. **Check the matcher** - Does it match the tool name? (e.g., "Bash", "Write", "Edit")
4. **Check hook type** - Is it "command", "prompt", or "agent"?
5. **Test the command** - Run the hook command manually to see if it works
6. **Use --debug** - Run `claude --debug` to see hook execution logs

content.text:
# Update Config Skill

Modify Claude Code configuration by updating settings.json files.

## When Hooks Are Required (Not Memory)

If the user wants something to happen automatically in response to an EVENT, they need a **hook** configured in settings.json. Memory/preferences cannot trigger automated actions.

**These require hooks:**
- "Before compacting, ask me what to preserve" → PreCompact hook
- "After writing files, run prettier" → PostToolUse hook with Write|Edit matcher
- "When I run bash commands, log them" → PreToolUse hook with Bash matcher
- "Always run tests after code changes" → PostToolUse hook

**Hook events:** PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, Stop, Notification, SessionStart

## CRITICAL: Read Before Write

**Always read the existing settings file before making changes.** Merge new settings with existing ones - never replace the entire file.

## CRITICAL: Use AskUserQuestion for Ambiguity

When the user's request is ambiguous, use AskUserQuestion to clarify:
- Which settings file to modify (user/project/local)
- Whether to add to existing arrays or replace them
- Specific values when multiple options exist

## Decision: /config command vs Direct Edit

**Suggest the `/config` slash command** for these simple settings:
- `theme`, `editorMode`, `verbose`, `model`
- `language`, `alwaysThinkingEnabled`
- `permissions.defaultMode`

**Edit settings.json directly** for:
- Hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.)
- Complex permission rules (allow/deny arrays)
- Environment variables
- MCP server configuration
- Plugin configuration

## Workflow

1. **Clarify intent** - Ask if the request is ambiguous
2. **Read existing file** - Use Read tool on the target settings file
3. **Merge carefully** - Preserve existing settings, especially arrays
4. **Edit file** - Use Edit tool (if file doesn't exist, ask user to create it first)
5. **Confirm** - Tell user what was changed

## Merging Arrays (Important!)

When adding to permission arrays or hook arrays, **merge with existing**, don't replace:

**WRONG** (replaces existing permissions):
```json
{ "permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(npm *)"] } }
```

**RIGHT** (preserves existing + adds new):
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(git *)",      // existing
      "Edit(.claude)",    // existing
      "Bash(npm *)"       // new
    ]
  }
}
```

## Settings File Locations

Choose the appropriate file based on scope:

| File | Scope | Git | Use For |
|------|-------|-----|---------|
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | Global | N/A | Personal preferences for all projects |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Project | Commit | Team-wide hooks, permissions, plugins |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | Project | Gitignore | Personal overrides for this project |

Settings load in order: user → project → local (later overrides earlier).

## Settings Schema Reference

### Permissions
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": ["Bash(npm *)", "Edit(.claude)", "Read"],
    "deny": ["Bash(rm -rf *)"],
    "ask": ["Edit(//etc/*)"],
    "defaultMode": "default" | "plan" | "acceptEdits" | "dontAsk",
    "additionalDirectories": ["/extra/dir"]
  }
}
```

**Permission Rule Syntax:**
- Exact match: `"Bash(npm run test)"`
- Prefix wildcard: `"Bash(git *)"` - matches `git`, `git status`, `git commit`, etc.
- Tool only: `"Read"` - allows all Read operations
- File paths: `"Edit(src/**)"` - path rules in `permissions` use `Edit(path)` for every file-writing tool (Write, Edit, NotebookEdit) and `Read(path)` for reads. `Write(path)`, `NotebookEdit(path)` and `Glob(path)` rules are not matched by file permission checks. Bare tool names (`"Write"`), deny/ask `Tool(param:value)` rules and hook `if` conditions still use each tool's own name

### Environment Variables
```json
{
  "env": {
    "DEBUG": "true",
    "MY_API_KEY": "value"
  }
}
```

### Model & Agent
```json
{
  "model": "sonnet",  // or "fable", "opus", "haiku", full model ID
  "agent": "agent-name",
  "alwaysThinkingEnabled": true
}
```

### Attribution (Commits & PRs)
```json
{
  "attribution": {
    "commit": "Custom commit trailer text",
    "pr": "Custom PR description text"
  }
}
```
Set `commit` or `pr` to empty string `""` to hide that attribution. To hide all of it, set both to `""` and also set `"sessionUrl": false`. Write this object form, not `"attribution": false`: older Claude Code versions reject true or false here and then skip the whole settings file.

### MCP Server Management
```json
{
  "enableAllProjectMcpServers": true,
  "enabledMcpjsonServers": ["server1", "server2"],
  "disabledMcpjsonServers": ["blocked-server"]
}
```

### Plugins
```json
{
  "enabledPlugins": {
    "formatter@anthropic-tools": true
  }
}
```
Plugin syntax: `plugin-name@source` where source is `claude-code-marketplace`, `claude-plugins-official`, or `builtin`.

### Other Settings
- `language`: Preferred response language (e.g., "japanese")
- `cleanupPeriodDays`: Days to keep transcripts before automatic cleanup (default: 30; minimum 1)
- `respectGitignore`: Whether to respect .gitignore (default: true)
- `spinnerTipsEnabled`: Show tips in spinner
- `timeFormat`: Clock format for times shown in the UI: "auto" (default), "12-hour", "24-hour", "24-hour-utc", or a strftime pattern such as "%H:%M"
- `timeZone`: IANA time zone for times shown in the UI, e.g. "UTC" (default: system time zone)
- `spinnerVerbs`: Customize spinner verbs (`{ "mode": "append" | "replace", "verbs": [...] }`)
- `spinnerTipsOverride`: Override spinner tips (`{ "excludeDefault": true, "tips": ["Custom tip"] }`)
- `syntaxHighlightingDisabled`: Disable diff highlighting


## Hooks Configuration

Hooks run commands at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle.

### Hook Structure
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "EVENT_NAME": [
      {
        "matcher": "ToolName|OtherTool",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "your-command-here",
            "timeout": 60,
            "statusMessage": "Running..."
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Hook Events

| Event | Matcher | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|
| PermissionRequest | Tool name | Run before permission prompt |
| PreToolUse | Tool name | Run before tool, can block |
| PostToolUse | Tool name | Run after successful tool |
| PostToolUseFailure | Tool name | Run after tool fails |
| Notification | Notification type | Run on notifications |
| Stop | - | Run when Claude stops (including clear, resume, compact) |
| PreCompact | "manual"/"auto" | Before compaction |
| PostCompact | "manual"/"auto" | After compaction (receives summary) |
| UserPromptSubmit | - | When user submits |
| SessionStart | - | When session starts |

**Common tool matchers:** `Bash`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`

### Hook Types

**1. Command Hook** - Runs a shell command:
```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "prettier --write $FILE", "timeout": 30 }
```

**2. Prompt Hook** - Evaluates a condition with LLM:
```json
{ "type": "prompt", "prompt": "Is this safe? $ARGUMENTS" }
```
Only available for tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.

**3. Agent Hook** - Runs an agent with tools:
```json
{ "type": "agent", "prompt": "Verify tests pass: $ARGUMENTS" }
```
Only available for tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.

### Hook Input (stdin JSON)
```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "tool_name": "Write",
  "tool_input": { "file_path": "/path/to/file.txt", "content": "..." },
  "tool_response": { "success": true }  // PostToolUse only
}
```

### Hook JSON Output

Hooks can return JSON to control behavior:

```json
{
  "systemMessage": "Warning shown to user in UI",
  "continue": false,
  "stopReason": "Message shown when blocking",
  "suppressOutput": false,
  "decision": "block",
  "reason": "Explanation for decision",
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
    "additionalContext": "Context injected back to model"
  }
}
```

**Fields:**
- `systemMessage` - Display a message to the user (all hooks)
- `continue` - Set to `false` to block/stop (default: true)
- `stopReason` - Message shown when `continue` is false
- `suppressOutput` - Hide stdout from transcript (default: false)
- `decision` - "block" for PostToolUse/Stop/UserPromptSubmit hooks (deprecated for PreToolUse, use hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision instead)
- `reason` - Explanation for decision
- `hookSpecificOutput` - Event-specific output (must include `hookEventName`):
  - `additionalContext` - Text injected into model context
  - `permissionDecision` - "allow", "deny", or "ask" (PreToolUse only)
  - `permissionDecisionReason` - Reason for the permission decision (PreToolUse only)
  - `updatedInput` - Modified tool input (PreToolUse only)

### Common Patterns

**Auto-format after writes:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_response.filePath // .tool_input.file_path' | { read -r f; prettier --write \"$f\"; } 2>/dev/null || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Log all bash commands:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Bash",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.command' >> ~/.claude/bash-log.txt"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Stop hook that displays message to user:**

Command must output JSON with `systemMessage` field:
```bash
# Example command that outputs: {"systemMessage": "Session complete!"}
echo '{"systemMessage": "Session complete!"}'
```

**Run tests after code changes:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_response.filePath' | grep -E '\\.(ts|js)$' && npm test || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```


## Constructing a Hook (with verification)

Given an event, matcher, target file, and desired behavior, follow this flow. Each step catches a different failure class — a hook that silently does nothing is worse than no hook.

1. **Dedup check.** Read the target file. If a hook already exists on the same event+matcher, show the existing command and ask: keep it, replace it, or add alongside.

2. **Construct the command for THIS project — don't assume.** The hook receives JSON on stdin. Build a command that:
   - Extracts any needed payload safely — use `jq -r` into a quoted variable or `{ read -r f; ... "$f"; }`, NOT unquoted `| xargs` (splits on spaces)
   - Invokes the underlying tool the way this project runs it (npx/bunx/yarn/pnpm? Makefile target? globally-installed?)
   - Skips inputs the tool doesn't handle (formatters often have `--ignore-unknown`; if not, guard by extension)
   - Stays RAW for now — no `|| true`, no stderr suppression. You'll wrap it after the pipe-test passes.

3. **Pipe-test the raw command.** Synthesize the stdin payload the hook will receive and pipe it directly:
   - `Pre|PostToolUse` on `Write|Edit`: `echo '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"<a real file from this repo>"}}' | <cmd>`
   - `Pre|PostToolUse` on `Bash`: `echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"ls"}}' | <cmd>`
   - `Stop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SessionStart`: most commands don't read stdin, so `echo '{}' | <cmd>` suffices

   Check exit code AND side effect (file actually formatted, test actually ran). If it fails you get a real error — fix (wrong package manager? tool not installed? jq path wrong?) and retest. Once it works, wrap with `2>/dev/null || true` (unless the user wants a blocking check).

4. **Write the JSON.** Merge into the target file (schema shape in the "Hook Structure" section above). If this creates `.claude/settings.local.json` for the first time, add it to .gitignore — the Write tool doesn't auto-gitignore it.

5. **Validate syntax + schema in one shot:**

   `jq -e '.hooks.<event>[] | select(.matcher == "<matcher>") | .hooks[] | select(.type == "command") | .command' <target-file>`

   Exit 0 + prints your command = correct. Exit 4 = matcher doesn't match. Exit 5 = malformed JSON or wrong nesting. A broken settings.json silently disables ALL settings from that file — fix any pre-existing malformation too.

6. **Prove the hook fires** — only for `Pre|PostToolUse` on a matcher you can trigger in-turn (`Write|Edit` via Edit, `Bash` via Bash). `Stop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SessionStart` fire outside this turn — skip to step 7.

   For a **formatter** on `PostToolUse`/`Write|Edit`: introduce a detectable violation via Edit (two consecutive blank lines, bad indentation, missing semicolon — something this formatter corrects; NOT trailing whitespace, Edit strips that before writing), re-read, confirm the hook **fixed** it. For **anything else**: temporarily prefix the command in settings.json with `echo "$(date) hook fired" >> /tmp/claude-hook-check.txt; `, trigger the matching tool (Edit for `Write|Edit`, a harmless `true` for `Bash`), read the sentinel file.

   **Always clean up** — revert the violation, strip the sentinel prefix — whether the proof passed or failed.

   **If proof fails but pipe-test passed and `jq -e` passed**: the settings watcher isn't watching `.claude/` — it only watches directories that had a settings file when this session started. The hook is written correctly. Tell the user to start a new session so the new settings load. You can't do this yourself.

7. **Handoff.** Tell the user the hook is live (or needs a new session per the watcher caveat), and that they can review, edit, or disable it later in the settings file you wrote. The UI only shows "Ran N hooks" if a hook errors or is slow — silent success is invisible by design.


## Example Workflows

### Adding a Hook

User: "Format my code after Claude writes it"

1. **Clarify**: Which formatter? (prettier, gofmt, etc.)
2. **Read**: `.claude/settings.json` (or create if missing)
3. **Merge**: Add to existing hooks, don't replace
4. **Result**:
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_response.filePath // .tool_input.file_path' | { read -r f; prettier --write \"$f\"; } 2>/dev/null || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

### Adding Permissions

User: "Allow npm commands without prompting"

1. **Read**: Existing permissions
2. **Merge**: Add `Bash(npm *)` to allow array
3. **Result**: Combined with existing allows

### Environment Variables

User: "Set DEBUG=true"

1. **Decide**: User settings (global) or project settings?
2. **Read**: Target file
3. **Merge**: Add to env object
```json
{ "env": { "DEBUG": "true" } }
```

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

1. **Replacing instead of merging** - Always preserve existing settings
2. **Wrong file** - Ask user if scope is unclear
3. **Invalid JSON** - Validate syntax after changes
4. **Forgetting to read first** - Always read before write

## Troubleshooting Hooks

If a hook isn't running:
1. **Check the settings file** - Read ~/.claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.json
2. **Verify JSON syntax** - Invalid JSON silently fails
3. **Check the matcher** - Does it match the tool name? (e.g., "Bash", "Write", "Edit")
4. **Check hook type** - Is it "command", "prompt", or "agent"?
5. **Test the command** - Run the hook command manually to see if it works
6. **Use --debug** - Run `claude --debug` to see hook execution logs

"""A regra que impede a sessao do Claude Code de ler o .env (que guarda a chave do provedor de LLM).

ISTO NAO PROVA QUE A REGRA FUNCIONA: quem aplica `.claude/settings.json` e o Claude Code, nao este repo, e a regra so vale numa sessao aberta
DEPOIS que o arquivo existe. O que o teste garante e o que e nosso: o arquivo existe, e JSON valido, nega Read/Edit/Bash do .env e das variantes,
e NAO nega o `.env.example` (que e versionado e precisa continuar legivel). Para verificar de verdade, ver o README (secao Dados sensiveis).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import fnmatch
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

SETTINGS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / ".claude" / "settings.json"


[EMAIL](scope="module")
def deny() -> list[str]:
    data = json.loads(SETTINGS.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    rules = data["permissions"]["deny"]
    assert all(isinstance(r, str) for r in rules)
    return rules


def rules_for(deny: list[str], tool: str) -> list[str]:
    return [m.group(1) for r in deny if (m := re.fullmatch(rf"{tool}\((.*)\)", r))]


def denied_path(deny: list[str], tool: str, path: str) -> bool:
    """Aproximacao do casamento de caminho (gitignore-style) com fnmatch: `**/x` casa `x` em qualquer pasta, inclusive a raiz."""
    for pat in rules_for(deny, tool):
        pat = pat.removeprefix("./")
        candidates = {pat, pat.removeprefix("**/")} if pat.startswith("**/") else {pat}
        if any(fnmatch.fnmatch(path, c) or fnmatch.fnmatch(path.removeprefix("./"), c) or fnmatch.fnmatch(Path(path).name, c) for c in candidates):
            return True
    return False


def denied_command(deny: list[str], command: str) -> bool:
    return any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(command, pat) for pat in rules_for(deny, "Bash"))


def test_the_settings_file_exists_and_is_valid_json():
    assert SETTINGS.exists(), ".claude/settings.json sumiu: a sessao voltaria a poder ler o .env"
    assert isinstance(json.loads(SETTINGS.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), dict)


[EMAIL]("path", [".env", "./.env", "autoseguro-agent/.env", "/abs/path/.env", ".env.local", "sub/.env.production", ".env.development"])

[EMAIL]("path", [".env.example", "./.env.example", "docs/.env.example", "README.md", "src/autoseguro/llm/config.py", "tests/fake_servers.py"])
def test_reading_other_files_including_the_example_stays_allowed(deny, path):
    assert not denied_path(deny, "Read", path), path


def test_overwriting_the_real_env_file_is_denied_but_not_the_example(deny):
    assert denied_path(deny, "Edit", ".env") and denied_path(deny, "Edit", "x/.env")
    assert not denied_path(deny, "Edit", ".env.example")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cria os commits da Etapa 2a por componente. Reexecutavel: `git reset -q eb84917` (mista, mantem a arvore) antes de rodar de novo.
set -euo pipefail
cd ~/dev/desafio-tecnico/autoseguro-agent
S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-[USUARIO]-dev-desafio-tecnico/eeb1d154-4766-4bcb-8673-8a9d3b2779c9/scratchpad/interm
TRAILER="Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <[EMAIL]>"

[ "$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)" = "eb84917" ] || { echo "HEAD nao e eb84917; faca git reset -q eb84917 antes"; exit 1; }
git reset -q   # indice limpo, arvore intacta

c() { # c "assunto" "porque" arquivos...
  local subject="$1" body="$2"; shift 2
  git add -- "$@"
  git commit -q -m "$subject" -m "$body" -m "$TRAILER"
  echo "ok  $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)  $subject"
}
blob() { git update-index --add --cacheinfo "100644,$(git hash-object -w "$2"),$1"; }

c "refactor(analysis): orçamentos de tempo numa fonte única e simulação do turno ponta a ponta" \
  "Os números de latência (5s/12s, 2,5s, 20s, 6s por chamada de LLM) estavam espalhados entre código, simulação e documentos. Agora vêm de budgets.py, e o limite por chamada de LLM é derivado do critério do turno, não escolhido." \
  src/autoseguro/budgets.py analysis/cost_model.py analysis/e2e_latency_sim.py analysis/latency_sim.py \
  analysis/results/cost_model.json analysis/results/cost_model.md analysis/results/e2e_latency_sim.json analysis/results/e2e_latency_sim.md \
  tests/test_budgets.py tests/test_analysis.py

c "feat(pii): detector compartilhado de PII e de segredos, inclusive a chave do OpenRouter" \
  "O gate que barra o que sai da máquina e o scanner de higiene do repo passam a usar os mesmos padrões, em src/autoseguro/pii.py. Entra o formato sk-or- porque a chave do provedor agora é do OpenRouter." \
  src/autoseguro/pii.py tests/pii_patterns.py tests/test_repo_hygiene.py

c "feat(handoff): componente que falhou é obrigatório em QUOTE_UNAVAILABLE e SAFETY_GUARD" \
  "A causa raiz decide o código, e o humano precisa saber qual parte falhou (quote_api ou llm). O pacote recusa esses dois motivos sem o componente." \
  src/autoseguro/handoff.py tests/doubles.py tests/test_handoff.py

c "feat(slots): normalização dos slots da cotação" \
  "A API aceita sem reclamar CEP ausente, CEP de 7 dígitos, plano vazio e data no passado, e devolve preço. Isso é preço errado em silêncio; a higiene tem que ser nossa, antes da chamada." \
  src/autoseguro/slots.py tests/test_slots.py

c "feat(guardrail): base de fatos do /planos e guardrail do reply do LLM" \
  "O LLM redige a conversa, mas só pode afirmar o que está numa base de fatos derivada do /planos, e nunca emite preço, prazo nem promessa. Reprovou, cai no template. O limite (frase falsa com termos autorizados) está registrado em teste." \
  src/autoseguro/facts.py src/autoseguro/guardrail.py tests/test_guardrail.py

c "feat(quote_client): cliente da /quote com política B, uma chamada em voo e relógio virtual" \
  "Timeout de 10s, retry só em falha transitória, orçamento de 15s, hedging descartado. O teste de que nunca há mais de uma chamada em voo é de comportamento, com um cliente defeituoso como controle negativo. Os testes de tempo usam relógio virtual, sem sleep." \
  src/autoseguro/quote_client.py tests/fakes.py tests/test_quote_client.py tests/integration/test_quote_client_real.py

c "feat(llm): esquema {slots, intent, facts_used, reply}, prompt estático e fast-path candidato" \
  "Uma única chamada extrai os slots e redige a resposta. O prompt é estático (sem data) para poder usar cache. O fast-path por regex nasce desligado e nada no produto o chama; o smoke mede a divergência." \
  src/autoseguro/llm/__init__.py src/autoseguro/llm/schema.py src/autoseguro/llm/prompt.py src/autoseguro/fastpath.py tests/test_llm_schema.py

  "O projeto não tem acesso à API direta da Anthropic, só ao OpenRouter (D4). A camada de LLM passa a ter uma interface, validação local da saída e configuração por LLM_PROVIDER/BASE_URL/API_KEY/MODEL. A chave do OpenRouter não pode passar pelo ClaudeLLM." \

  "Chat completions com response_format json_schema e provider.require_parameters, raciocínio desligado por padrão e erros tratados (inclusive dentro de um 200). Testado contra um servidor local falso, sem rede." \
  src/autoseguro/llm/openai_compat.py tests/test_openai_compat.py

c "feat(llm): ClaudeLLM como adaptador opcional atrás da mesma interface" \
  "A API da Anthropic continua como opção, com o SDK só no extra llm. O adaptador recusa apontar para o OpenRouter, porque usa parâmetros da Anthropic que o OpenRouter não garante." \
  src/autoseguro/llm/claude.py tests/test_claude_llm.py pyproject.toml

c "feat(llm): limite de taxa, cota diária contada e backoff, com falha rápida em erro de protocolo" \
  "Free tier do OpenRouter: 20 req/min e 50/dia. Toda requisição é contada, inclusive as que falham, porque a documentação não diz se elas contam. O primeiro erro de protocolo (4xx fora 408 e 429) interrompe na hora e custa uma requisição; só 429 e 5xx entram em backoff, e um disjuntor impede um serviço fora do ar de comer a cota." \
  src/autoseguro/llm/throttle.py tests/test_throttle.py

c "feat(llm): GuardedLLM e fábrica única, com o gate de PII e o guardrail acima de qualquer adaptador" \
  "Trocar de provedor não pode contornar o gate nem o guardrail, então eles ficam fora dos adaptadores e a fábrica só devolve LLM embrulhado. O teste roda nos dois adaptadores e tem controle negativo (o adaptador cru enviaria a PII)." \
  src/autoseguro/llm/guarded.py src/autoseguro/llm/factory.py tests/test_llm_layers.py

c "feat(llm): causa provável de cada falha, por código e configuração" \
  "Quando o pedido é recusado, o usuário precisa saber o que conferir (a chave, o json_schema, o raciocínio, o modelo) sem ler o corpo do erro. O texto nunca recebe nem imprime a chave." \
  src/autoseguro/llm/diagnose.py tests/test_diagnose.py

c "feat(tools): smoke-llm com 15 mensagens escritas à mão, dentro do free tier" \
  "É o maior risco do plano e foi antecipado para antes da 2b. 1 modelo, 2 repetições, 31 requisições. Aborta antes de gastar se a cota não cobre, e falha rápido no primeiro erro de protocolo. A chave nunca aparece em saída, log nem relatório." \
  tools/__init__.py tools/smoke_llm.py tools/smoke_messages.py tests/test_smoke.py tests/test_smoke_quota.py tests/conftest.py

c "feat(tools): llm-ping, preflight de uma requisição antes do smoke" \
  "Como não sabemos se requisição que falha conta na cota, descobrir que o OpenRouter não aceita o pedido (json_schema + require_parameters) tem que custar uma requisição, não 31. Confere autenticação, pedido, saída válida e a latência da amostra, e mostra só 'chave: configurada'." \
  tools/llm_ping.py tests/test_llm_ping.py tests/test_key_safety.py

blob README.md "$S/README.md"
c "docs: D4 no README, PLAN com o OpenRouter, .env.example e alvos do Makefile" \
  "Registra a troca de provedor como decisão (D4), com o que foi conferido na documentação do OpenRouter e o que não foi. O .env.example e o Makefile (llm-ping, smoke-llm) acompanham." \
  docs/PLAN.md .env.example Makefile

c "chore: nega à sessão do Claude Code a leitura do .env, que guarda a chave do provedor" \
  "Regra de deny em .claude/settings.json (Read, Edit e padrões de Bash). Vale só em sessão aberta depois do arquivo, não foi confirmada na que a criou e não é uma barreira contra comando que lê o arquivo sem citá-lo; o README diz isso, e um teste impede a regra de sumir ou de bloquear o .env.example." \
  .claude/settings.json tests/test_claude_settings.py README.md

echo "--- arvore restante:"; git status --short
