tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to [EMAIL]' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "autoseguro-agent"
version = "0.0.0"
description = "Agente de cotacao de seguro auto (desafio FDE Namastex)"
# Verificado em 3.12 (container, mesma base do servico de cotacao) e 3.14 (host). Nao declaramos o que nao testamos.
requires-python = ">=3.12"
# Dependencias de runtime entram junto com a etapa que as usa (ver docs/PLAN.md).
dependencies = []

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest>=8"]
analysis = ["pandas>=2.2", "pyarrow>=15"]
llm = ["anthropic>=1.15,<2"]  # so o ClaudeLLM e o smoke-llm; o mock e os testes nao precisam dele

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = [".", "src"]  # "src": cada checkout testa o proprio codigo, sem depender de `pip install -e`
testpaths = ["tests"]
addopts = "-ra"
markers = [
    "integration: precisa da API de cotacao no ar (make test-integration)",
    "contract: compara o codigo com a API real (make test-integration)",
    "llm_real: chama a API da Anthropic (opt-in; precisa de ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)",
]
----
# Preferimos o Python do container da API (3.12) por paridade; cai para o que existir (>= 3.12).
PYTHON ?= $(shell command -v python3.12 || command -v python3.13 || command -v python3.14)
VENV   ?= .venv
BIN    := $(VENV)/bin

# O parquet e dado externo (nao vai no repo). O padrao assume o clone do desafio ao lado deste repo.
DATASET_PATH ?= ../namastex-fde-challenge/dataset/conversations.parquet
export DATASET_PATH

.PHONY: help setup test test-integration api-up api-down api-test-up api-test-down chat demo analysis-dataset analysis-latency analysis-e2e analysis-cost llm-ping smoke-llm smoke-llm-anthropic smoke-llm-dry

help: ## lista os alvos
	@grep -E '^[a-z-]+:.*## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | sed -E 's/:.*## /\t/'

setup: ## cria o venv e instala dev + analysis
	@test -n "$(PYTHON)" || (echo "precisa de Python >= 3.12"; exit 1)
	$(PYTHON) -m venv $(VENV)
	$(BIN)/pip install -q -e ".[dev,analysis,llm]"

test: ## testes unitarios e de higiene (nao precisam da API; a checagem do dataset roda se DATASET_PATH existir)
	$(BIN)/pytest -m "not integration and not contract and not llm_real"

test-integration: api-test-up ## sobe a API de teste (porta 8100, sem falhas) e roda os testes que a usam
	$(BIN)/pytest -m "integration or contract"

api-up: ## API com a instabilidade padrao do desafio (porta 8000)
	docker compose up --build -d --wait

api-down:
	docker compose down

api-test-up: ## API deterministica para testes (porta 8100, falha e lentidao zeradas)
	docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml up --build -d --wait

api-test-down:
	docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml down

chat: ## conversa no terminal (MockLLM, offline). ARGS="--api http://localhost:8100" aponta a API de teste; ARGS="--llm real" usa o modelo do .env (gasta a cota do provedor)
	$(BIN)/python -m autoseguro $(ARGS)

demo: api-test-up ## os quatro cenarios (cotacao, recusa, /quote fora do ar, pedido de humano) com o MockLLM e a API de teste; grava var/scenarios/
	$(BIN)/python tools/scenarios.py

llm-ping: ## preflight de 1 requisicao real: autenticacao, pedido aceito (json_schema + require_parameters), saida valida e latencia da amostra. Rode antes do smoke-llm
	$(BIN)/python tools/llm_ping.py $(ARGS)

smoke-llm: ## mede o LLM real: 15 mensagens escritas a mao, sem PII, 1 modelo, 2 repeticoes = 31 requisicoes, dentro do limite diario que o provedor informa (LLM_API_KEY ou OPENROUTER_API_KEY em .env)
	$(BIN)/python tools/smoke_llm.py $(ARGS)

smoke-llm-anthropic: ## o mesmo smoke pela API direta da Anthropic (ClaudeLLM). Opcional: instala o SDK e precisa de LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
	$(BIN)/pip install -q -e ".[llm]"
	LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic $(BIN)/python tools/smoke_llm.py $(ARGS)

smoke-llm-dry: ## o mesmo encanamento com um LLM de mentira: sem chave e sem rede
	$(BIN)/python tools/smoke_llm.py --dry-run $(ARGS)

analysis-dataset: ## perfil agregado do dataset -> analysis/results/dataset_profile.json
	$(BIN)/python -I analysis/dataset_profile.py --parquet $(DATASET_PATH) --out analysis/results/dataset_profile.json

analysis-latency: ## simulacao das politicas de cliente -> analysis/results/latency_sim.{json,md}
	$(BIN)/python -I analysis/latency_sim.py --out analysis/results

analysis-e2e: ## latencia fim a fim (LLM + /quote); a latencia do LLM e hipotese -> analysis/results/e2e_latency_sim.{json,md}
	$(BIN)/python -I analysis/e2e_latency_sim.py --out analysis/results

analysis-cost: ## custo por conversa (tokens estimados, precos da skill claude-api) -> analysis/results/cost_model.{json,md}
	$(BIN)/python -I analysis/cost_model.py --out analysis/results

"""Quem escreve o reply: o LLM na conversa NEUTRA, o TEMPLATE nas intencoes de RISCO.

Regex nao julga sentido. O smoke de 2026-10-20 mostrou dois replies de risco que o guardrail aprovou e que enganam a olho: "Sim, mas ha
carencia" a quem perguntou se roubo amanha esta coberto, e "a melhor opcao da AutoSeguro" numa objecao de preco. Caçar esses padroes
com mais regex e perder a corrida; entao, nas intencoes de risco, o texto que o lead le NAO vem do LLM:

  RISCO (template, montado dos fatos): duvida de carencia ou cobertura, objecao de preco, sinistro, pedido de humano, reclamacao, cancelamento,
  e o lead querer fechar. O LLM NAO REDIGE NADA QUE LEVE A UM HANDOFF: toda intencao que e motivo de handoff esta aqui (testado contra o enum).
  NEUTRA (LLM, com o guardrail R1-R7 estrito): saudacao, proxima pergunta, confirmacao.

Do LLM, nas turnos de risco, vale so a INTENCAO. Por isso reconhecer a intencao de risco passou a ser criterio do smoke (100%): se o
modelo classifica uma duvida de carencia como `provide_info`, o reply livre dele chega ao lead, ainda sob o guardrail.

Cada reply de risco tem um CORPO (so fatos e frases fixas, e passa no `check_reply` por construcao, testado) e, se houver, uma PERGUNTA do
produto (`questions.py`) para o orquestrador seguir a conversa. A objecao de preco segue o fluxo do PLAN: oferece UMA alternativa real;
se o lead hesita de novo, handoff PRICE_OBJECTION. Nunca promete desconto.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

from . import questions
from .facts import COVERAGE_IDS, COVERAGE_LABEL, FactBase
from .handoff import HandoffReason
from .llm.guarded import GuardedResult
from .quote_client import Quote
from .store import brl

# `question_not_in_facts` entra porque e uma duvida de cobertura que os fatos nao respondem: a resposta honesta e fixa.
RISK_INTENTS = frozenset({"ask_coverage_question", "question_not_in_facts", "price_objection", "claim", "wants_human", "complaint", "cancel",
                          "ready_to_close"})

# Intencao -> motivo de handoff. A objecao de preco so vira handoff na 2a hesitacao (ou sem alternativa), por isso sai daqui e fica em `_risk`.
HANDOFF_BY_INTENT = {"wants_human": HandoffReason.HUMAN_REQUESTED, "claim": HandoffReason.CLAIM_SINISTRO, "complaint": HandoffReason.COMPLAINT,
                     "cancel": HandoffReason.CANCELLATION, "ready_to_close": HandoffReason.READY_TO_CLOSE}

NOT_IN_FACTS = "Não tenho essa informação por aqui, e prefiro não chutar."
NOT_UNDERSTOOD = "Não consegui entender direito. Pode escrever de outro jeito?"
PRICE_OFFER = "Entendo que o valor pesou. Posso te mostrar outro plano para você comparar?"
CLAIM = "Sinto muito pelo que aconteceu. Acionar o seguro (sinistro) não é comigo: eu só faço cotação."
COMPLAINT = "Sinto muito pela experiência."
CANCEL = "Entendi que você quer cancelar. Cancelamento não é comigo: eu só faço cotação."
CLOSE = "Que bom que você quer seguir! A emissão da apólice e a contratação não são comigo: eu só faço cotação."
_HANDOFF_LEAD_IN = {"wants_human": "Claro.", "claim": CLAIM, "complaint": COMPLAINT, "cancel": CANCEL, "ready_to_close": CLOSE}


def handoff_text(next_step: str = "") -> str:
    """O que o lead le quando a conversa passa a um humano (D2): honesto, sem prazo, canal nem desconto. `next_step` e configuracao de negocio."""
    base = "Um consultor vai dar continuidade à sua conversa, e o que você me contou ficou registrado."
    return f"{base} {next_step.strip()}" if next_step.strip() else base


# --- templates de COTACAO, RECUSA e HANDOFF: carregam numero e promessa, entao nenhum texto aqui vem do LLM -------------------------------------------
HOLD_TEXT = "Um instante, estou calculando a sua cotação."
UNAVAILABLE = ("Não consegui gerar a sua cotação agora por uma instabilidade no nosso sistema, e não vou te passar valor sem a confirmação dele.")
LLM_DOWN = "Estou com uma instabilidade e não consigo continuar a conversa agora."
SAFETY = "Não consegui processar a sua mensagem com segurança."
DATA_UNCONFIRMED = "Não consegui confirmar os seus dados para montar a cotação."
AFTER_HANDOFF = "Sua conversa já está com um consultor, que vai dar continuidade. O que você me contou ficou registrado."
CLOSED_REFUSED = "Esta conversa foi encerrada porque não consigo cotar este perfil. Obrigado pelo interesse!"
NO_QUOTE_YET = "Ainda não montei a sua cotação. Me passa os dados que eu calculo e você já vê o valor."
OFF_TOPIC = "Isso foge do que eu consigo ajudar: eu só faço cotação de seguro de carro."
AFTER_QUOTE = "Se algum dado estiver errado, ou se quiser comparar outro plano, é só me dizer."


def _labels(items) -> str:
    names = [COVERAGE_LABEL.get(c, c) for c in items]
    return names[0] if len(names) == 1 else ", ".join(names[:-1]) + " e " + names[-1]


def render_quote(q: Quote, verified: dict[str, str], *, alternative: bool = False) -> str:
    """A mensagem de cotacao. TODO valor em reais sai de um numero da resposta da API (`Quote`); o recap repete os dados usados, para o lead ver se algo esta errado."""
    lines = [f"Aqui está a cotação do plano {q.plano_nome}" + (" (outra opção para você comparar)" if alternative else "") + ":",
             f"• Mensalidade: {brl(q.premio_mensal)}"]
    if q.primeiro_pagamento is not None and q.pro_rata:
        lines.append(f"• Primeiro pagamento: {brl(q.primeiro_pagamento)} (proporcional: {q.pro_rata.get('dias_cobrados')} de {q.pro_rata.get('dias_no_mes')} dias do mês)")
    lines += [f"• Franquia: {brl(q.franquia)}",
              f"• Cobre: {_labels(q.coberturas)}",
              f"• Carência: {_labels(q.carencia_coberturas)} só passam a valer {q.carencia_dias} dias depois do início da vigência."]
    recap = questions.recap(verified, q.plano_nome)
    return "\n".join(lines + ([recap] if recap else []) + ["Se algum dado estiver errado, me avisa que eu refaço."])


def render_refusal(motivo: str) -> str:
    return f"Não consigo cotar este perfil: {motivo.strip().rstrip('.')}. Por isso vou encerrar por aqui. Obrigado pelo interesse!"


def failure_handoff_text(reason: HandoffReason, next_step: str = "") -> str:
    """O texto do handoff de FALHA (o orquestrador decide o motivo; o texto e sempre template, honesto e sem promessa)."""
    lead_in = {HandoffReason.QUOTE_UNAVAILABLE: UNAVAILABLE, HandoffReason.SAFETY_GUARD: SAFETY, HandoffReason.DATA_AMBIGUOUS: DATA_UNCONFIRMED}.get(reason, "")
    return f"{lead_in} {handoff_text(next_step)}".strip()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reply:
    text: str                                    # o que o lead le (corpo + pergunta)
    source: str                                  # "llm" | "template_risk" | "template_fallback"
    body: str = ""                               # so o corpo montado dos fatos / frases fixas (o que passa no guardrail por construcao)
    question: str | None = None                  # a pergunta do produto que segue o corpo
    facts_used: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    action: str | None = None                    # None | "offer_alternative" | "handoff"
    handoff_reason: HandoffReason | None = None
    violations: tuple[str, ...] = ()             # por que o reply do LLM foi trocado pelo template (so no fallback)


_PLAN_WORDS = re.compile(r"\bplanos?\b")


def facts_for_question(text: str, base: FactBase) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Os fatos que respondem a pergunta do lead, escolhidos pelo TEXTO DELE com o mesmo lexico do guardrail, nao pela citacao do modelo
    (que uma injecao poderia manipular). No maximo dois. Vazio = a base nao responde."""
    terms = base.find_terms(text)
    picked: list[str] = []

    def add(fid: str) -> None:
        if fid in base.facts and fid not in picked:
            picked.append(fid)

    if terms & {"carencia", "roubo", "furto"}:
        add("carencia")
    if "franquia" in terms:
        add("franquia")
    if "pro_rata" in terms:
        add("pro_rata")
    named = [t for t in terms if t.startswith("plan_")]
    for t in sorted(named):
        add("plano:" + t[len("plan_"):])
    wanted = (terms & COVERAGE_IDS) - {"roubo", "furto"}
    if wanted and not named:  # "cobre vidros?": os dois planos mais baratos que cobrem
        covering = sorted((t for t, cov in base.plan_coverages.items() if wanted <= cov), key=lambda t: len(base.plan_coverages[t]))
        for t in covering[:2]:
            add("plano:" + t[len("plan_"):])
    if not picked and _PLAN_WORDS.search(text.lower()):
        add("planos")
    return tuple(picked[:2])


def price_handoff(next_step: str = "") -> Reply:
    """A objecao de preco que sobrou (2a hesitacao, recusa da alternativa ou nenhum plano mais barato): um humano pode negociar, o agente nao promete nada."""
    body = f"Entendo. {handoff_text(next_step)}"
    return Reply(body, "template_risk", body, action="handoff", handoff_reason=HandoffReason.PRICE_OBJECTION)


def _coverage(lead_text: str, cited: tuple[str, ...], base: FactBase, question: str | None) -> Reply:
    ids = facts_for_question(lead_text, base) or tuple(f for f in cited if f in base.facts)[:2]  # sem match no texto, vale o que o modelo citou
    if not ids:
        return Reply(_join(NOT_IN_FACTS, question), "template_risk", NOT_IN_FACTS, question)
    body = " ".join(base.facts[f].text for f in ids)
    return Reply(_join(body, question), "template_risk", body, question, facts_used=ids)


def _join(body: str, question: str | None) -> str:
    return f"{body} {question}" if question else body


def select_reply(gres: GuardedResult, base: FactBase, *, lead_text: str, next_question: str | None = None, objection_count: int = 0,
                 has_alternative: bool = True, handoff_next_step: str = "") -> Reply:
    """O reply que vai ao lead. `next_question`: a pergunta do produto para o passo seguinte (o orquestrador a escolhe pelo estado).
    `objection_count`: quantas objecoes de preco ANTES desta. `has_alternative`: ha um plano mais barato para oferecer?"""
    fallback_q = next_question or NOT_UNDERSTOOD
    out = gres.output
    if out is None:  # falha do LLM, saida invalida, bloqueio do provedor: a conversa nao fica sem resposta
        return Reply(fallback_q, "template_fallback", fallback_q, violations=("sem_saida",))
    if out.intent in RISK_INTENTS:
        return _risk(out.intent, lead_text, out.facts_used, base, next_question, objection_count, has_alternative, handoff_next_step)
    if gres.reply_ok:
        return Reply(out.reply, "llm", out.reply, facts_used=out.facts_used)
    return Reply(fallback_q, "template_fallback", fallback_q, violations=tuple(sorted({v.rule for v in gres.violations})))


def _risk(intent: str, lead_text: str, cited: tuple[str, ...], base: FactBase, next_question: str | None, objection_count: int,
          has_alternative: bool, handoff_next_step: str) -> Reply:
    if intent == "ask_coverage_question":
        return _coverage(lead_text, cited, base, next_question)
    if intent == "question_not_in_facts":
        return Reply(_join(NOT_IN_FACTS, next_question), "template_risk", NOT_IN_FACTS, next_question)
    if intent == "price_objection":
        if objection_count == 0 and has_alternative:
            return Reply(PRICE_OFFER, "template_risk", PRICE_OFFER, action="offer_alternative")
        return price_handoff(handoff_next_step)
    body = f"{_HANDOFF_LEAD_IN[intent]} {handoff_text(handoff_next_step)}"  # claim, wants_human, complaint, cancel, ready_to_close
    return Reply(body, "template_risk", body, action="handoff", handoff_reason=HANDOFF_BY_INTENT[intent])

"""Mascarador de PII: roda ANTES de qualquer texto do lead ir ao LLM ou ao banco. O texto cru nao sai da funcao que o recebe.

Troca o que identifica uma pessoa por um marcador ([CPF], [EMAIL], [TELEFONE], [PLACA], [NOME], [NASCIMENTO], [CAMINHO], [SEGREDO]) e DEIXA
INTACTO o que a cotacao precisa: CEP, ano do carro, idade e data de inicio. Cobre mais formatos que o detector de `pii.py` (CPF sem pontuacao, telefone
com parenteses, placa antiga), que continua sendo o gate de envio: o mascarador reduz, o gate confere, e o que o gate ainda achar e SAFETY_GUARD.

LIMITE ASSUMIDO (PLAN, secao 14): e um PISO, nao uma garantia. Regex e uma lista de nomes conhecidos nao pegam todo nome proprio nem todo endereco.
O que nao e reconhecido passa; por isso o texto cru nunca e persistido e o gate roda por cima de tudo.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Iterable
from dataclasses import dataclass

from .pii import find_pii

_CPF_PUNCT = re.compile(r"(?<!\d)\d{3}\.\d{3}\.\d{3}-\d{2}(?!\d)")
_ELEVEN_DIGITS = re.compile(r"(?<!\d)\d{11}(?!\d)")
_EMAIL = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9-]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9-]+)+")
# Telefone: +55 opcional, DDD OBRIGATORIO (com ou sem parenteses), 9 opcional, 4 + 4 digitos. Sem DDD "2015 2016" (dois anos digitados juntos) viraria telefone,
# e um CEP (5-3 digitos) nunca casa: falta o segundo bloco de 4. O celular sem DDD ("91234-5678") tem o padrao proprio abaixo.
_PHONE = re.compile(r"(?<![\d-])(?:\+?55[\s.-]?)?(?:\(\s*\d{2}\s*\)|\d{2})[\s.-]?9?\d{4}[\s.-]?\d{4}(?![\d-])")
_LOCAL_PHONE = re.compile(r"(?<![\d-])9\d{4}-\d{4}(?![\d-])")
_PLACA = re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z]{3}-?\d[A-Za-z0-9]\d{2}\b")
_HOME = re.compile(r"~/\S*")
_SECRET = re.compile(r"sk-(?:ant|or)-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{6,}|(?i:bearer)\s+[A-Za-z0-9_\-.=]{8,}")
_NAME = re.compile(r"(?i:\b(?:meu nome (?:é|e)|me chamo|sou (?:o|a)|aqui (?:é|e) (?:o|a))\s+)"
                   r"([A-ZÀ-Ý][\wÀ-ÿ]+(?:\s+(?:d[aeo]s?\s+)?[A-ZÀ-Ý][\wÀ-ÿ]+){0,3})")
_BIRTHDATE = re.compile(r"(?i:\bnasc\w*\W{0,3}(?:em\W{0,3}|no dia\W{0,3}|dia\W{0,3})?)(\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{2,4})")


def cpf_is_valid(digits: str) -> bool:
    """Digitos verificadores do CPF. Separa um CPF de 11 digitos de um telefone de 11 digitos sem pontuacao."""
    if len(digits) != 11 or len(set(digits)) == 1:
        return False
    for n in (9, 10):
        s = sum(int(d) * w for d, w in zip(digits[:n], range(n + 1, 1, -1), strict=True))
        if int(digits[n]) != (s * 10 % 11) % 10:
            return False
    return True


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Masked:
    text: str
    kinds: tuple[str, ...]   # QUE tipos foram mascarados (nunca o trecho)


class Masker:
    def __init__(self, known_names: Iterable[str] = ()) -> None:
        self._names = tuple(sorted({n.strip() for n in known_names if n and len(n.strip()) >= 3}, key=len, reverse=True))

    def mask(self, text: str) -> Masked:
        kinds: list[str] = []

        def sub(rx: re.Pattern[str], token: str, s: str, kind: str, group: int | None = None) -> str:
            def repl(m: re.Match[str]) -> str:
                kinds.append(kind)
                if group is None:
                    return token
                return m.group(0)[:m.start(group) - m.start(0)] + token + m.group(0)[m.end(group) - m.start(0):]
            return rx.sub(repl, s)

        out = text
        out = sub(_SECRET, "[SEGREDO]", out, "segredo")
        out = sub(_HOME, "[CAMINHO]", out, "caminho")
        out = sub(_EMAIL, "[EMAIL]", out, "email")

    terms = base.find_terms(text)
    picked: list[str] = []

    def add(fid: str) -> None:
        if fid in base.facts and fid not in picked:

    if terms & {"carencia", "roubo", "furto"}:
        add("carencia")
    if "franquia" in terms:
        add("franquia")
    if "pro_rata" in terms:
        add("pro_rata")
    named = [t for t in terms if t.startswith("plan_")]
    for t in sorted(named):

    if wanted and not named:  # "cobre vidros?": os dois planos mais baratos que cobrem
        covering = sorted((t for t, cov in base.plan_coverages.items() if wanted <= cov), key=lambda t: len(base.plan_coverages[t]))
        for t in covering[:2]:

    if not ids:
        return Reply(_join(NOT_IN_FACTS, question), "template_risk", NOT_IN_FACTS, question)
    body = " ".join(base.facts[f].text for f in ids)
    return Reply(_join(body, question), "template_risk", body, question, facts_used=ids)

    fallback_q = next_question or NOT_UNDERSTOOD
    out = gres.output
    if out is None:  # falha do LLM, saida invalida, bloqueio do provedor: a conversa nao fica sem resposta
        return Reply(fallback_q, "template_fallback", fallback_q, violations=("sem_saida",))
    if out.intent in RISK_INTENTS:
        return _risk(out.intent, lead_text, out.facts_used, base, next_question, objection_count, has_alternative, handoff_next_step)
    if gres.reply_ok:
        return Reply(out.reply, "llm", out.reply, facts_used=out.facts_used)
    return Reply(fallback_q, "template_fallback", fallback_q, violations=tuple(sorted({v.rule for v in gres.violations})))

"""Mascarador de PII: roda ANTES de qualquer texto do lead ir ao LLM ou ao banco. O texto cru nao sai da funcao que o recebe.

Troca o que identifica uma pessoa por um marcador ([CPF], [EMAIL], [TELEFONE], [PLACA], [NOME], [NASCIMENTO], [CAMINHO], [SEGREDO]) e DEIXA
INTACTO o que a cotacao precisa: CEP, ano do carro, idade e data de inicio. Cobre mais formatos que o detector de `pii.py` (CPF sem pontuacao, telefone
com parenteses, placa antiga), que continua sendo o gate de envio: o mascarador reduz, o gate confere, e o que o gate ainda achar e SAFETY_GUARD.

LIMITE ASSUMIDO (PLAN, secao 14): e um PISO, nao uma garantia. Regex e uma lista de nomes conhecidos nao pegam todo nome proprio nem todo endereco.
O que nao e reconhecido passa; por isso o texto cru nunca e persistido e o gate roda por cima de tudo.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Iterable
from dataclasses import dataclass

from .pii import find_pii

_CPF_PUNCT = re.compile(r"(?<!\d)\d{3}\.\d{3}\.\d{3}-\d{2}(?!\d)")
_ELEVEN_DIGITS = re.compile(r"(?<!\d)\d{11}(?!\d)")
_EMAIL = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9-]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9-]+)+")
# Telefone: +55 opcional, DDD OBRIGATORIO (com ou sem parenteses), 9 opcional, 4 + 4 digitos. Sem DDD "2015 2016" (dois anos digitados juntos) viraria telefone,
# e um CEP (5-3 digitos) nunca casa: falta o segundo bloco de 4. O celular sem DDD ("91234-5678") tem o padrao proprio abaixo.
_PHONE = re.compile(r"(?<![\d-])(?:\+?55[\s.-]?)?(?:\(\s*\d{2}\s*\)|\d{2})[\s.-]?9?\d{4}[\s.-]?\d{4}(?![\d-])")
_LOCAL_PHONE = re.compile(r"(?<![\d-])9\d{4}-\d{4}(?![\d-])")
_PLACA = re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z]{3}-?\d[A-Za-z0-9]\d{2}\b")
_HOME = re.compile(r"~/\S*")
_SECRET = re.compile(r"sk-(?:ant|or)-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{6,}|(?i:bearer)\s+[A-Za-z0-9_\-.=]{8,}")
_NAME = re.compile(r"(?i:\b(?:meu nome (?:é|e)|me chamo|sou (?:o|a)|aqui (?:é|e) (?:o|a))\s+)"
                   r"([A-ZÀ-Ý][\wÀ-ÿ]+(?:\s+(?:d[aeo]s?\s+)?[A-ZÀ-Ý][\wÀ-ÿ]+){0,3})")
_BIRTHDATE = re.compile(r"(?i:\bnasc\w*\W{0,3}(?:em\W{0,3}|no dia\W{0,3}|dia\W{0,3})?)(\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{2,4})")


def cpf_is_valid(digits: str) -> bool:
    """Digitos verificadores do CPF. Separa um CPF de 11 digitos de um telefone de 11 digitos sem pontuacao."""
    if len(digits) != 11 or len(set(digits)) == 1:
        return False
    for n in (9, 10):
        s = sum(int(d) * w for d, w in zip(digits[:n], range(n + 1, 1, -1), strict=True))
        if int(digits[n]) != (s * 10 % 11) % 10:
            return False
    return True


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Masked:
    text: str
    kinds: tuple[str, ...]   # QUE tipos foram mascarados (nunca o trecho)


class Masker:
    def __init__(self, known_names: Iterable[str] = ()) -> None:
        self._names = tuple(sorted({n.strip() for n in known_names if n and len(n.strip()) >= 3}, key=len, reverse=True))

    def mask(self, text: str) -> Masked:
        kinds: list[str] = []

        def sub(rx: re.Pattern[str], token: str, s: str, kind: str, group: int | None = None) -> str:
            def repl(m: re.Match[str]) -> str:
                kinds.append(kind)
                if group is None:
                    return token
                return m.group(0)[:m.start(group) - m.start(0)] + token + m.group(0)[m.end(group) - m.start(0):]
            return rx.sub(repl, s)

        out = text
        out = sub(_SECRET, "[SEGREDO]", out, "segredo")
        out = sub(_HOME, "[CAMINHO]", out, "caminho")
        out = sub(_EMAIL, "[EMAIL]", out, "email")
        out = sub(_CPF_PUNCT, "[CPF]", out, "cpf")
        out = _ELEVEN_DIGITS.sub(lambda m: self._eleven(m.group(0), kinds), out)
        out = sub(_BIRTHDATE, "[NASCIMENTO]", out, "nascimento", group=1)
        out = sub(_PHONE, "[TELEFONE]", out, "telefone")
        out = sub(_LOCAL_PHONE, "[TELEFONE]", out, "telefone")
        out = sub(_PLACA, "[PLACA]", out, "placa")
        out = sub(_NAME, "[NOME]", out, "nome", group=1)

Um PISO, nao uma garantia: ele so enxerga os formatos abaixo. CPF sem pontuacao, telefone com parenteses e placa antiga
ficam para o mascarador da Etapa 2b, que tem teste proprio.

from __future__ import annotations

import re

PATTERNS = {
    "cpf": re.compile(r"\b\d{3}\.\d{3}\.\d{3}-\d{2}\b"),
    "email": re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9-]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9-]+)+"),
    "telefone_br": re.compile(r"\+55 ?\d{2} ?9\d{4}-?\d{4}"),
    "placa_mercosul": re.compile(r"\b[A-Z]{3}\d[A-Z]\d{2}\b"),
    "caminho_de_home": re.compile(r"~/"),
    "chave_anthropic": re.compile(r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}"),
    "chave_openrouter": re.compile(r"sk-or-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}"),
}
EMAIL_OK_DOMAINS = ("example.com", "example.org")


def find_pii(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Tipos de PII/segredo encontrados em `text` (sem o trecho: quem chama nao deve reimprimir o achado)."""
    kinds = []
    for kind, rx in PATTERNS.items():
        for m in rx.finditer(text):
            if kind == "email" and m.group(0).lower().endswith(EMAIL_OK_DOMAINS):
                continue
            kinds.append(kind)
            break
    return kinds

"""Higiene do repo: PII, segredos e linhas cruas do dataset.

As mensagens de falha mostram arquivo, linha e TIPO do achado, nunca o trecho: o teste nao pode vazar o que cobre.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from tests.pii_patterns import EMAIL_OK_DOMAINS, PATTERNS

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

def _findings(files: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> list[str]:
    out = []
    for rel, text in files:
        for n, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
            for kind, rx in PATTERNS.items():
                for m in rx.finditer(line):
                    if kind == "email" and m.group(0).lower().endswith(EMAIL_OK_DOMAINS):
                        continue
                    out.append(f"{rel}:{n} [{kind}]")
    return out


def test_no_pii_or_secrets_in_repo(repo_text_files):
    found = _findings(repo_text_files)
    assert not found, "PII/segredo em arquivos do repo (trecho omitido de proposito):\n" + "\n".join(found[:30])


def test_pii_scanner_catches_what_it_should():
    """Guarda do guarda: se o scanner parar de enxergar, a higiene acima vira teatro."""
    # Amostras montadas em tempo de execucao: o literal completo nao pode existir na fonte deste arquivo.
    samples = ["111.222" + ".333-44", "a" + "@" + "b.com", "+55 11 9" + "1234-5678", "ABC1" + "D23",
               "/Users" + "/fulano/x", "sk-ant" + "-abcdefgh12", "sk-or" + "-v1-abcdefgh12"]
    fake = [("x.txt", ", ".join(samples))]
    kinds = {f.split("[")[1].rstrip("]") for f in _findings(fake)}
    assert kinds == set(PATTERNS)


def test_no_raw_dataset_lines_in_repo(dataset_bodies, repo_text_files):
    haystacks = [(rel, text.lower()) for rel, text in repo_text_files]
    leaks = sorted({rel for rel, text in haystacks for body in dataset_bodies if body in text})
    assert not leaks, f"trechos de mensagens do dataset encontrados em: {leaks}"

As mensagens de falha mostram arquivo, linha e TIPO do achado, nunca o trecho: o teste nao pode vazar o que cobre.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from tests.pii_patterns import EMAIL_OK_DOMAINS, PATTERNS

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

def _findings(files: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> list[str]:
    out = []
    for rel, text in files:
        for n, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
            for kind, rx in PATTERNS.items():
                for m in rx.finditer(line):
                    if kind == "email" and m.group(0).lower().endswith(EMAIL_OK_DOMAINS):
                        continue
                    out.append(f"{rel}:{n} [{kind}]")
    return out


def test_no_pii_or_secrets_in_repo(repo_text_files):
    found = _findings(repo_text_files)
    assert not found, "PII/segredo em arquivos do repo (trecho omitido de proposito):\n" + "\n".join(found[:30])


def test_pii_scanner_catches_what_it_should():
    """Guarda do guarda: se o scanner parar de enxergar, a higiene acima vira teatro."""
    # Amostras montadas em tempo de execucao: o literal completo nao pode existir na fonte deste arquivo.
    samples = ["111.222" + ".333-44", "a" + "@" + "b.com", "+55 11 9" + "1234-5678", "ABC1" + "D23",
               "/Users" + "/fulano/x", "sk-ant" + "-abcdefgh12", "sk-or" + "-v1-abcdefgh12"]
    fake = [("x.txt", ", ".join(samples))]
    kinds = {f.split("[")[1].rstrip("]") for f in _findings(fake)}
    assert kinds == set(PATTERNS)


def test_no_raw_dataset_lines_in_repo(dataset_bodies, repo_text_files):
    haystacks = [(rel, text.lower()) for rel, text in repo_text_files]
    leaks = sorted({rel for rel, text in haystacks for body in dataset_bodies if body in text})
    assert not leaks, f"trechos de mensagens do dataset encontrados em: {leaks}"

"""Fabrica da camada de LLM: a UNICA porta de entrada do produto para um cliente de LLM.

Devolve sempre um `GuardedLLM` (gate de PII + guardrail por fora de qualquer adaptador). Trocar `LLM_PROVIDER` troca o adaptador e nao
contorna nenhuma protecao. Os adaptadores continuam importaveis (os testes os exercitam), mas o produto so os obtem por aqui.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from ..facts import FactBase
from .base import LLMClient
from .claude import ClaudeLLM
from .config import ConfigError, LLMConfig
from .guarded import GuardedLLM
from .openai_compat import OpenAICompatLLM

_LOCAL_HOSTS = ("localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1")


def make_adapter(cfg: LLMConfig, fact_base: FactBase, *, client: Any = None) -> LLMClient:
    if cfg.provider == "anthropic":
        return ClaudeLLM(cfg.model, fact_base, client=client, api_key=cfg.api_key, max_tokens=cfg.max_tokens, timeout_s=cfg.timeout_s,
                         base_url=cfg.base_url)
    local = (urlparse(cfg.base_url or "").hostname or "") in _LOCAL_HOSTS
    if not cfg.api_key and not local:
        raise ConfigError(cfg.missing_key_message())
    return OpenAICompatLLM(cfg.model, fact_base, base_url=cfg.base_url or "", api_key=cfg.api_key, provider=cfg.provider,
                           structured_output=cfg.structured_output, reasoning_effort=cfg.reasoning_effort, max_tokens=cfg.max_tokens,
                           timeout_s=cfg.timeout_s, temperature=cfg.temperature)


def make_llm(cfg: LLMConfig, fact_base: FactBase, *, wrap: Callable[[LLMClient], LLMClient] | None = None, client: Any = None) -> GuardedLLM:
    """`wrap`: decorador opcional ENTRE o adaptador e o guarda (ex.: `ThrottledLLM` para o free tier). O guarda e sempre o mais externo."""
    adapter = make_adapter(cfg, fact_base, client=client)
    return GuardedLLM(wrap(adapter) if wrap else adapter, fact_base)

As amostras de PII (sinteticas) ficam em tests/fixtures/pii_samples/masker.json, a unica pasta que o scanner de higiene do repo ignora."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import random
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from autoseguro.anchoring import read_text
from autoseguro.masker import Masker, cpf_is_valid, residual_pii
from autoseguro.pii import find_pii

FIX = json.loads((Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "pii_samples" / "masker.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
V = FIX["values"]
CASES = [(c["raw"].format(**V), c["token"], c["kind"]) for c in FIX["cases"]]
VALID_CPF, VALID_CPF_DIGITS = V["cpf"], V["cpf_digits"]
M = Masker()


[EMAIL]("raw,token,kind", CASES)
def test_what_identifies_a_person_is_replaced_by_a_marker(raw, token, kind):
    r = M.mask(raw)
    assert token in r.text and kind in r.kinds
    assert residual_pii(r.text) == [], r.text


def test_known_names_are_masked_case_insensitively_and_only_as_whole_words():
    r = Masker(known_names=["Beltrano Souza", "Souza"]).mask("oi, aqui é o beltrano souza, mas o souzado não")
    assert r.text.count("[NOME]") == 1 and "souzado" in r.text and "nome" in r.kinds


def test_a_cpf_with_invalid_check_digits_is_not_called_a_cpf_but_is_still_masked_as_a_phone():
    assert not cpf_is_valid("11111111111") and not cpf_is_valid(V["cpf_bad_digits"]) and cpf_is_valid(VALID_CPF_DIGITS)
    r = M.mask(V["eleven_not_cpf"])
    assert r.text == "[TELEFONE]" and r.kinds == ("telefone",)

"""Logica de cotacao. Le plans.json e aplica as regras (faixa etaria, idade do
veiculo, regiao, carencia, pro-rata de entrada no meio do mes)."""
from __future__ import annotations
import json, datetime as dt
from pathlib import Path
from calendar import monthrange

_PLANS_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data" / "plans.json"


def load_plans() -> dict:
    return json.loads(_PLANS_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


class CotacaoRecusada(Exception):
    def __init__(self, motivo: str):
        self.motivo = motivo
        super().__init__(motivo)


def _faixa_etaria_mult(regras: dict, idade: int) -> float:
    for f in regras["faixa_etaria"]:
        if f["idade_min"] <= idade <= f["idade_max"]:
            if f.get("recusar"):
                raise CotacaoRecusada(f["motivo"])
            return f["multiplicador"]
    raise CotacaoRecusada("Idade fora das faixas aceitas.")


def _idade_veiculo_mult(regras: dict, ano_veiculo: int, hoje: dt.date) -> float:
    anos = hoje.year - ano_veiculo
    for f in regras["idade_veiculo"]:
        if f["anos_min"] <= anos <= f["anos_max"]:
            if f.get("recusar"):
                raise CotacaoRecusada(f["motivo"])
            return f["multiplicador"]
    raise CotacaoRecusada("Idade do veiculo fora das faixas aceitas.")


def _regiao_mult(regras: dict, cep: str | None) -> float:
    if not cep:
        return 1.0
    pref = cep.replace("-", "").strip()[:2]
    r = regras["regiao_cep"]
    return r["multiplicador"] if pref in r["prefixos_alto_risco"] else 1.0


def _pro_rata_primeiro_mes(base_mensal: float, inicio: dt.date) -> dict:
    """Primeiro mes proporcional aos dias restantes (inclui o dia de inicio)."""
    dias_mes = monthrange(inicio.year, inicio.month)[1]
    dias_restantes = dias_mes - inicio.day + 1
    valor = round(base_mensal * dias_restantes / dias_mes, 2)
    return {"dias_no_mes": dias_mes, "dias_cobrados": dias_restantes, "valor_primeiro_pagamento": valor}


def cotar(payload: dict) -> dict:
    """Recebe dados do lead/veiculo e devolve a cotacao calculada.
    Campos esperados: plano_id, idade (int), veiculo_ano (int),
    cep (str, opcional), data_inicio (YYYY-MM-DD, opcional)."""
    plans = load_plans()
    regras = plans["regras"]
    hoje = dt.date.today()

    plano_id = (payload.get("plano_id") or "essencial").lower()
    plano = next((p for p in plans["planos"] if p["id"] == plano_id), None)
    if plano is None:
        raise CotacaoRecusada(f"Plano '{plano_id}' inexistente. Opcoes: "
                              + ", ".join(p["id"] for p in plans["planos"]))

    idade = int(payload["idade"])
    ano = int(payload["veiculo_ano"])
    cep = payload.get("cep")

    m_idade = _faixa_etaria_mult(regras, idade)
    m_veic = _idade_veiculo_mult(regras, ano, hoje)
    m_regiao = _regiao_mult(regras, cep)

    premio = round(plano["base_mensal"] * m_idade * m_veic * m_regiao, 2)

    car = regras["carencia"]
    resp = {
        "plano_id": plano["id"],
        "plano_nome": plano["nome"],
        "premio_mensal": premio,
        "franquia": plano["franquia"],
        "coberturas": plano["coberturas"],
        "multiplicadores": {"faixa_etaria": m_idade, "idade_veiculo": m_veic, "regiao": m_regiao},
        "carencia": {
            "coberturas": [c for c in plano["coberturas"] if c in car["coberturas_com_carencia"]],
            "dias": car["dias"],
            "observacao": car["_obs"],
        },
        "moeda": plans["moeda"],
    }

    di = payload.get("data_inicio")
    if di:
        inicio = dt.date.fromisoformat(di)
        if inicio.day != 1:
            resp["primeiro_pagamento_pro_rata"] = _pro_rata_primeiro_mes(premio, inicio)
    return resp
"""
Servico de cotacao de seguro auto (mock) para o desafio FDE.

POST /quote  -> calcula uma cotacao a partir dos dados do lead/veiculo.
GET  /health -> health check (sempre estavel).
GET  /planos -> tabela de planos e regras (consulta).

Observacao de operacao: este servico simula um sistema legado real. Ele NEM SEMPRE
responde de primeira -- parte das chamadas falha ou demora. Trate isso no seu agente.
A taxa e a latencia sao configuraveis por variavel de ambiente:
    QUOTE_FAILURE_RATE   (default 0.20)  -> fracao de chamadas que falham
    QUOTE_SLOW_RATE      (default 0.10)  -> fracao de chamadas lentas
    QUOTE_SLOW_SECONDS   (default 8)     -> duracao da chamada lenta (simula timeout)
    QUOTE_SEED           (opcional)      -> fixa o gerador p/ falhas reproduziveis
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import os, time, random
from fastapi import FastAPI, Response
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from .quote_logic import cotar, load_plans, CotacaoRecusada

FAILURE_RATE = float(os.getenv("QUOTE_FAILURE_RATE", "0.20"))
SLOW_RATE = float(os.getenv("QUOTE_SLOW_RATE", "0.10"))
SLOW_SECONDS = float(os.getenv("QUOTE_SLOW_SECONDS", "8"))
_seed = os.getenv("QUOTE_SEED")
_rng = random.Random(int(_seed)) if _seed else random.Random()

app = FastAPI(title="AutoSeguro Quote API (mock)", version="1.0.0")


class QuoteRequest(BaseModel):
    plano_id: str = Field("essencial", description="essencial | completo | premium")
    idade: int = Field(..., ge=0, le=200)
    veiculo_ano: int = Field(..., ge=1950, le=2100)
    cep: str | None = None
    data_inicio: str | None = Field(None, description="YYYY-MM-DD (opcional)")


[EMAIL]("/health")
def health():
    return {"status": "ok"}


[EMAIL]("/planos")
def planos():
    return load_plans()


[EMAIL]("/quote")
def quote(req: QuoteRequest):
    # --- instabilidade simulada (de proposito) ---
    roll = _rng.random()
    if roll < FAILURE_RATE:
        kind = _rng.choice(["500", "502", "503"])
        return JSONResponse(status_code=int(kind),
                            content={"error": "upstream_unavailable",
                                     "message": "Servico de cotacao temporariamente indisponivel. Tente novamente."})
    if roll < FAILURE_RATE + SLOW_RATE:
        time.sleep(SLOW_SECONDS)  # simula timeout / lentidao

    # --- cotacao ---
    try:
        return cotar(req.model_dump())
    except CotacaoRecusada as e:
        return JSONResponse(status_code=422, content={"error": "cotacao_recusada", "motivo": e.motivo})
    except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as e:
        return JSONResponse(status_code=400, content={"error": "payload_invalido", "detalhe": str(e)})

# Análises

Scripts que sustentam `docs/FINDINGS.md` e `docs/PLAN.md`. Regras do projeto:

- A saída é **só agregado** (números e rótulos de enum). Nenhum texto de mensagem do dataset é impresso ou gravado.
- O parquet é dado externo: não está no repo. O caminho vem de `DATASET_PATH` (padrão do Makefile: o clone do desafio ao lado deste repo).
- Rode com `python -I` (modo isolado) e passe caminhos como argumento.

## Scripts

| Script | O que faz | Como rodar |
|---|---|---|
| `dataset_profile.py` | Perfil agregado do dataset (estrutura, timestamps, vazamento de colunas, elegibilidade, PII, preço do vendedor vs API, sinal do desfecho) | `make analysis-dataset` |
| `latency_sim.py` | Monte Carlo das políticas de cliente A, B e C | `make analysis-latency` |
| `e2e_latency_sim.py` | Latência por mensagem somando LLM e `/quote`. **A latência do LLM é hipótese**, e o script varre o p50 para mostrar onde cada critério quebra | `make analysis-e2e` |
| `cost_model.py` | Tokens e dólares por conversa, por modelo e por política de cache. **Tokens são estimativa; preços são da tabela da skill `claude-api`** | `make analysis-cost` |
| `api_probe.py` | Sondagem do comportamento do `/quote` (precisa da API no ar) | ver abaixo |

As regras de elegibilidade e preço são lidas de `vendor/quote-service/data/plans.json`, não copiadas para os scripts.

## `api_probe.py`: qual instância usar

Cada modo precisa de uma configuração diferente da API. As saídas que estão em `results/` foram geradas assim:

| Modo | Instância | Saída |
|---|---|---|
| `rules --port 8100` | `make api-test-up` (sem falha e sem lentidão) | `results/api_probe_rules.txt` |
| `outage --port N` | container com `QUOTE_FAILURE_RATE=1` | `results/api_probe_outage.txt` |
| `seq --port N` | container com `QUOTE_SEED=42`, `QUOTE_FAILURE_RATE=0.5`, `QUOTE_SLOW_RATE=0` (rodado duas vezes, com restart) | `results/api_probe_seed.txt` |
| `stats --port N` | container com a instabilidade padrão (0,20 / 0,10 / 8s), 400 chamadas, 30 em paralelo | `results/api_probe_stats.txt` |

Os containers descartáveis usam a imagem `autoseguro-quote-api:local` (criada por `make api-test-up`):

```bash
docker run -d --rm --name qprobe-down -p 8101:8000 -e QUOTE_FAILURE_RATE=1 -e QUOTE_SLOW_RATE=0 autoseguro-quote-api:local
```

Datas e anos de veículo da sondagem são relativos a hoje, então o script continua válido quando virar o ano.
Os arquivos de `results/` registram a data em que foram gerados.
['structure', 'ordering', 'conversation_level_columns_replicated', 'vehicle_and_age', 'pii', 'vendor_price_vs_api', 'outcome_signal', 'diversity_and_missing_scenarios']

# Dicionário de dados — `conversations.parquet`

> ⚠️ **Dados 100% sintéticos.** Conversas, nomes, CPF, e-mails, telefones, placas e CEPs
> foram **gerados proceduralmente** (`scripts/generate_dataset.py`). Os formatos são
> plausíveis, mas **nenhum dado é de pessoa real**. Ainda assim, trate-os como se fossem
> sensíveis — é parte do desafio.

Cada **linha = uma mensagem**. Conversas se reconstroem agrupando por `conversation_id`
e ordenando por `message_index`.

| Coluna | Tipo | Descrição |
|---|---|---|
| `conversation_id` | string | Identificador da conversa (`conv_00001`, ...) |
| `message_index` | int | Ordem da mensagem dentro da conversa (0 = primeira) |
| `timestamp` | string (ISO 8601) | Horário da mensagem |
| `sender_role` | string | `lead` ou `vendedor` |
| `sender_name` | string | Nome exibido do remetente |
| `message_type` | string | `text`, `image`, `audio` ou `document` |
| `message_body` | string | Conteúdo. Para mídia, vem um marcador (ex.: `[LINHA DO DATASET REDIGIDA]`) |
| `channel` | string | Sempre `whatsapp` |
| `conversation_outcome` | string | Desfecho: `ganho`, `perdido`, `em_negociacao`, `sem_resposta` |
| `lead_idade_informada` | int | Idade que o lead informou (quando aplicável) |
| `veiculo_texto` | string | Marca/modelo/ano em texto livre, como o lead falou |

## Notas

- O conteúdo das mensagens é **não estruturado** — dados como CPF, e-mail, telefone e placa
  aparecem soltos no meio do texto, em formatos variados.
- Algumas mensagens são de **mídia** (`image`/`audio`/`document`): não há transcrição, só o marcador.
- `veiculo_texto` é texto livre ("[LINHA DO DATASET REDIGIDA]", "Toyota [LINHA DO DATASET REDIGIDA]") — não vem normalizado.
- Regenerar (reprodutível): `uv run scripts/generate_dataset.py --n 2500 --seed 42`.
